all_evidence.title: Effectiveness of Iron Supplementation With or Without Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agents on Red Blood Cell Utilization in Patients With Preoperative Anaemia Undergoing Elective Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Van Remoortel H; Laermans J; Avau B; Bekkering G; Georgsen J; Manzini PM; Meybohm P; Ozier Y; De Buck E; Compernolle V; Vandekerckhove P
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: Patient Blood Management (PBM) is an evidence-based, multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to optimizing the care of patients who might need a blood transfusion. | Primary outcomes were the number of patients and the number of RBC units transfused. | We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 연구 결과는 다음과 같았다. (1) IV 및/또는 경구 철분 단독요법은 수혈 단위 수를 줄이지 않을 수 있으며, IV 철분은 수혈받는 환자 수를 줄이지 않을 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (2) 철분요법의 투여 경로(IV vs 경구)가 RBC 사용량에 서로 다른 영향을 미치는지는 불확실하다(근거 확실성 매우 낮음). (3) IV 카르복시말토스제이철 단독요법은 IV 철 자당 단독요법과 비교할 때 수혈받는 환자 수에 차이를 만들지 않을 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (4) 경구 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받는 환자 수와 수혈 단위 수를 줄일 가능성이 높다(근거 확실성 중간). (5) IV 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받는 환자 수를 줄일 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (6) 경구 및/또는 IV 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받은 환자에서 수혈된 RBC 단위 수를 줄일 가능성이 높다(근거 확실성 중간). (7) 경구 및/또는 IV 철분 + ESAs가 여러 단위의 수혈이 필요한 환자 수에 미치는 영향은 불확실하다(근거 확실성 매우 낮음).
all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
all_evidence.population: This systematic review aimed to collect the best available evidence on the effectiveness of preoperative iron supplementation with or without erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) on red blood cell (RBC) utilization in all-cause anaemic patients scheduled for elective surgery. | We identified 29 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 2 non-RCTs comparing the effectiveness of preoperative iron monotherapy, or iron + ESAs, to control (no treatment, usual care, placebo). | In conclusion, in patients with anaemia of any cause scheduled for elective surgery, the preoperative administration of iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of patients or units transfused (low-certainty evidence).

all_evidence.title: Perioperative omega-3 fatty acids for liver surgery: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.authors: Xiao F; Han W; Yue Q; Ke J; Jia B; Fu X
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: Overall, compared with control group for liver surgery, omega-3 fatty acids were associated with substantially reduced incidence of infection (odd ratio [OR]=0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] =0.34-0.91; P = .02), but revealed no remarkable influence on complications (OR = 0.60; 95% CI = 0.29-1.24; P = .17), mortality (OR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.06-9.37; P = .83), liver failure (OR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.10 to 5.00; P = 0.74), biliary leakage (OR=1.24; 95% CI = 0.41 to 3.76; P = .70), bleeding (OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 0.63-4.95; P = .28), or ileus (OR = 0.39; 95% CI = 0.07-2.05; P = .27).
all_evidence.outcome: Overall, compared with control group for liver surgery, omega-3 fatty acids were associated with substantially reduced incidence of infection (odd ratio [OR]=0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] =0.34-0.91; P = .02), but revealed no remarkable influence on complications (OR = 0.60; 95% CI = 0.29-1.24; P = .17), mortality (OR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.06-9.37; P = .83), liver failure (OR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.10 to 5.00; P = 0.74), biliary leakage (OR=1.24; 95% CI = 0.41 to 3.76; P = .70), bleeding (OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 0.63-4.95; P = .28), or ileus (OR = 0.39; 95% CI = 0.07-2.05; P = .27).
all_evidence.key_finding: Overall, compared with control group for liver surgery, omega-3 fatty acids were associated with substantially reduced incidence of infection (odd ratio [OR]=0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] =0.34-0.91; P = .02), but revealed no remarkable influence on complications (OR = 0.60; 95% CI = 0.29-1.24; P = .17), mortality (OR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.06-9.37; P = .83), liver failure (OR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.10 to 5.00; P = 0.74), biliary leakage (OR=1.24; 95% CI = 0.41 to 3.76; P = .70), bleeding (OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 0.63-4.95; P = .28), or ileus (OR = 0.39; 95% CI = 0.07-2.05; P = .27).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 전체적으로 간 수술 대조군과 비교했을 때 오메가-3 지방산은 감염 발생률을 상당히 낮추는 것과 관련이 있었지만(odds ratio [OR]=0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] =0.34-0.91; P = .02), 합병증(OR = 0.60; 95% CI = 0.29-1.24; P = .17), 사망(OR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.06-9.37; P = .83), 간부전(OR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.10 to 5.00; P = 0.74), 담즙 누출(OR=1.24; 95% CI = 0.41 to 3.76; P = .70), 출혈(OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 0.63-4.95; P = .28), 장폐색(OR = 0.39; 95% CI = 0.07-2.05; P = .27)에는 뚜렷한 영향을 보이지 않았다.
all_evidence.population: INTRODUCTION: The effect of perioperative omega-3 fatty acids for liver surgery remained controversial. | We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to explore the influence of omega-3 fatty acids versus placebo in patients undergoing liver surgery. | METHODS: We have searched PubMed, EMbase, Web of science, EBSCO, and Cochrane library databases through May 2020, and included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing the effect of omega-3 fatty acids versus placebo for liver surgery.

all_evidence.title: Effects of intraoperative or postoperative administration of intravenous iron supplements on hemoglobin recovery in patients with total knee arthroplasty: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Kwak SG; Kwon JB; Bae JW; Bae DJ; Kim DK; Choi WK
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: CONCLUSION: The administration of IV iron supplements during or after TKA surgery increases hemoglobin recovery between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery and reduces the need for allogeneic blood transfusion during hospitalization.
all_evidence.outcome: Second, to examine whether the administration of IV iron supplements during or immediately after TKA in patients undergoing primary TKA can reduce the need for allogenic blood transfusion during hospitalization. | The population, intervention, comparison, and outcome of this study are as follows; Population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty; Intervention: Administration of IV iron supplements during or immediately after surgery; Comparison: Non-administration of IV iron supplements; Outcome: Degree of hemoglobin recovery (between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery) and the need for blood transfusion during hospitalization. | There was a statistically significant difference for post-operative transfusion rate between 2 groups.
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSION: The administration of IV iron supplements during or after TKA surgery increases hemoglobin recovery between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery and reduces the need for allogeneic blood transfusion during hospitalization.

all_evidence.key_finding: METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299.

all_evidence.title: Comprehensive preoperative regime of selective gut decontamination in combination with probiotics, and smectite for reducing endotoxemia and cytokine activation during cardiopulmonary bypass: A pilot randomized, controlled trial.
all_evidence.authors: Liu WC; Zhan YP; Wang XH; Hou BC; Huang J; Chen SB
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: RESULTS: The mean levels of change in endotoxin levels after CPB in patients receiving the comprehensive preoperative regimen was marginally significantly lower than those in control group (F = 4.0, P = .0552) but was not significantly different for procalcitonin (F = .14, P = .7134).

all_evidence.title: Preoperative Sucrosomial Iron Supplementation Increases Haemoglobin and Reduces Transfusion Requirements in Elective Heart Surgery Patients: A Prospective Randomized Study.

all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Low preoperative haemoglobin is frequently observed in heart surgery patients and is associated with a significant decrease in haemoglobin between post-operative days 2 and 3, known as haemoglobin drift. | STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: The purpose of this study was to assess whether preoperative supplementation with oral sucrosomial iron, a new iron-delivery technology with improved tolerance and bioavailability, might be an effective strategy for this patient population. | One thousand consecutive patients were randomized and received either a one-month course of sucrosomial iron (60 mg/day) or no treatment prior to elective heart surgery at a single high-volume centre (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03560687).

all_evidence.title: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Preoperative Antithrombin Supplementation in Patients at Risk for Antithrombin Deficiency After Cardiac Surgery.

all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Multicenter Study|Randomized Controlled Trial|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
all_evidence.population: Preoperative AT supplementation, to achieve >58% and <100% AT activity, may potentially reduce postoperative morbidity and mortality in cardiac operations with CPB. | This prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study was designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of preoperative treatment with AT supplementation in patients at risk for low AT activity after undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. | METHODS: A total of 425 adult patients were randomized (1:1) to receive either a single dose of AT (n = 213) to achieve an absolute increase of 20% above pretreatment AT activity or placebo (n = 212) before surgery.

all_evidence.title: Risk factors for bleeding and perioperative bleeding complications in oculoplastic surgery: a prospective pilot study.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).

all_evidence.key_finding: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_2: METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299.
all_evidence.outcome: METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299.
all_evidence.key_finding: METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299.

all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Early enteral nutrition with solutions containing prebiotics (fiber) and probiotics (Lactobacillus) is suggested to reduce bacterial translocation and minimize the incidence of infections after liver transplantation. | METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299. | RESULTS: The groups were comparable regarding preoperative American Society of Anesthesiologists classification, Child-Pugh classification of cirrhosis, operative data, and degree of immunosuppression.

all_evidence.title: Preoperative Sucrosomial Iron Supplementation Increases Haemoglobin and Reduces Transfusion Requirements in Elective Heart Surgery Patients: A Prospective Randomized Study.

all_evidence.outcome: Overall, these patients tend to receive many RBC transfusions. | Primary end-points were haemoglobin concentration on the day of hospital admittance and number of blood transfusions. | The percentage of patients in the treatment group who required transfusion (35.4%) was half that in the control group (64.6%).
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSION: In elective heart surgery, routine preoperative sucrosomial iron administration seems to be a safe, well-tolerated and cost-effective strategy to increase preoperative haemoglobin and reduce the need for allogeneic blood transfusions.

all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Low preoperative haemoglobin is frequently observed in heart surgery patients and is associated with a significant decrease in haemoglobin between post-operative days 2 and 3, known as haemoglobin drift. | STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: The purpose of this study was to assess whether preoperative supplementation with oral sucrosomial iron, a new iron-delivery technology with improved tolerance and bioavailability, might be an effective strategy for this patient population. | One thousand consecutive patients were randomized and received either a one-month course of sucrosomial iron (60 mg/day) or no treatment prior to elective heart surgery at a single high-volume centre (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03560687).

all_evidence.title: Risk factors for bleeding and perioperative bleeding complications in oculoplastic surgery: a prospective pilot study.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Clear guidelines for managing patients on antiplatelet (AP) or anticoagulant (AC) therapy undergoing oculoplastic surgery are lacking. | This study investigates bleeding risk factors and evaluates the effectiveness of a standardised bleeding risk assessment in extraocular surgery. | METHODS: In this prospective study, a standardised questionnaire (SQ) was employed to gather patients' bleeding histories.
all_evidence.key_finding: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).

evidence.title: Effectiveness of Iron Supplementation With or Without Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agents on Red Blood Cell Utilization in Patients With Preoperative Anaemia Undergoing Elective Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.authors: Van Remoortel H; Laermans J; Avau B; Bekkering G; Georgsen J; Manzini PM; Meybohm P; Ozier Y; De Buck E; Compernolle V; Vandekerckhove P
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
evidence.outcome: Patient Blood Management (PBM) is an evidence-based, multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to optimizing the care of patients who might need a blood transfusion. | Primary outcomes were the number of patients and the number of RBC units transfused. | We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
evidence.key_finding: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 연구 결과는 다음과 같았다. (1) IV 및/또는 경구 철분 단독요법은 수혈 단위 수를 줄이지 않을 수 있으며, IV 철분은 수혈받는 환자 수를 줄이지 않을 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (2) 철분요법의 투여 경로(IV vs 경구)가 RBC 사용량에 서로 다른 영향을 미치는지는 불확실하다(근거 확실성 매우 낮음). (3) IV 카르복시말토스제이철 단독요법은 IV 철 자당 단독요법과 비교할 때 수혈받는 환자 수에 차이를 만들지 않을 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (4) 경구 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받는 환자 수와 수혈 단위 수를 줄일 가능성이 높다(근거 확실성 중간). (5) IV 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받는 환자 수를 줄일 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (6) 경구 및/또는 IV 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받은 환자에서 수혈된 RBC 단위 수를 줄일 가능성이 높다(근거 확실성 중간). (7) 경구 및/또는 IV 철분 + ESAs가 여러 단위의 수혈이 필요한 환자 수에 미치는 영향은 불확실하다(근거 확실성 매우 낮음).
evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
evidence.population: This systematic review aimed to collect the best available evidence on the effectiveness of preoperative iron supplementation with or without erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) on red blood cell (RBC) utilization in all-cause anaemic patients scheduled for elective surgery. | We identified 29 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 2 non-RCTs comparing the effectiveness of preoperative iron monotherapy, or iron + ESAs, to control (no treatment, usual care, placebo). | In conclusion, in patients with anaemia of any cause scheduled for elective surgery, the preoperative administration of iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of patients or units transfused (low-certainty evidence).

evidence.title: Early enteral supply of lactobacillus and fiber versus selective bowel decontamination: a controlled trial in liver transplant recipients.
evidence.authors: Rayes N; Seehofer D; Hansen S; Boucsein K; Müller AR; Serke S; Bengmark S; Neuhaus P
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_2: METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299.
evidence.outcome: METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299.
evidence.key_finding: METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 방법: 95명의 환자로 구성된 전향적 무작위 위약 대조 시험에서 모든 군에 조기 경장영양을 제공하고 간 이식 후 수술 후 감염과 기타 합병증 발생률을 세 군 간 비교했다. 세 군은 (a) 표준 조제식 + 선택적 장 오염 제거(SBD), (b) 섬유 함유 조제식 + 살아 있는 Lactobacillus plantarum 299, (c) 섬유 함유 조제식 + 열처리로 사멸시킨 L plantarum 299였다.
evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Early enteral nutrition with solutions containing prebiotics (fiber) and probiotics (Lactobacillus) is suggested to reduce bacterial translocation and minimize the incidence of infections after liver transplantation. | METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299. | RESULTS: The groups were comparable regarding preoperative American Society of Anesthesiologists classification, Child-Pugh classification of cirrhosis, operative data, and degree of immunosuppression.

all_evidence.title: Effectiveness of Iron Supplementation With or Without Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agents on Red Blood Cell Utilization in Patients With Preoperative Anaemia Undergoing Elective Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Van Remoortel H; Laermans J; Avau B; Bekkering G; Georgsen J; Manzini PM; Meybohm P; Ozier Y; De Buck E; Compernolle V; Vandekerckhove P
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: Patient Blood Management (PBM) is an evidence-based, multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to optimizing the care of patients who might need a blood transfusion. | Primary outcomes were the number of patients and the number of RBC units transfused. | We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 연구 결과는 다음과 같았다. (1) IV 및/또는 경구 철분 단독요법은 수혈 단위 수를 줄이지 않을 수 있으며, IV 철분은 수혈받는 환자 수를 줄이지 않을 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (2) 철분요법의 투여 경로(IV vs 경구)가 RBC 사용량에 서로 다른 영향을 미치는지는 불확실하다(근거 확실성 매우 낮음). (3) IV 카르복시말토스제이철 단독요법은 IV 철 자당 단독요법과 비교할 때 수혈받는 환자 수에 차이를 만들지 않을 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (4) 경구 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받는 환자 수와 수혈 단위 수를 줄일 가능성이 높다(근거 확실성 중간). (5) IV 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받는 환자 수를 줄일 수 있다(근거 확실성 낮음). (6) 경구 및/또는 IV 철분 + ESAs는 수혈받은 환자에서 수혈된 RBC 단위 수를 줄일 가능성이 높다(근거 확실성 중간). (7) 경구 및/또는 IV 철분 + ESAs가 여러 단위의 수혈이 필요한 환자 수에 미치는 영향은 불확실하다(근거 확실성 매우 낮음).
all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
all_evidence.population: This systematic review aimed to collect the best available evidence on the effectiveness of preoperative iron supplementation with or without erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) on red blood cell (RBC) utilization in all-cause anaemic patients scheduled for elective surgery. | We identified 29 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 2 non-RCTs comparing the effectiveness of preoperative iron monotherapy, or iron + ESAs, to control (no treatment, usual care, placebo). | In conclusion, in patients with anaemia of any cause scheduled for elective surgery, the preoperative administration of iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of patients or units transfused (low-certainty evidence).

all_evidence.title: Risk factors for bleeding and perioperative bleeding complications in oculoplastic surgery: a prospective pilot study.
all_evidence.authors: Christensen NA; Feltgen N; Horn M; Naxer S; van Oterendorp C; Koscielny J; Sucker C; Pfeiffer S; Kück F; Schittkowski MP
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Clear guidelines for managing patients on antiplatelet (AP) or anticoagulant (AC) therapy undergoing oculoplastic surgery are lacking. | This study investigates bleeding risk factors and evaluates the effectiveness of a standardised bleeding risk assessment in extraocular surgery. | METHODS: In this prospective study, a standardised questionnaire (SQ) was employed to gather patients' bleeding histories.
all_evidence.key_finding: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 출혈 합병증은 더 높은 SQ 점수(p=0.048), 눈꺼풀 수술에서의 아세틸살리실산 사용(p=0.038), 당뇨병(p=0.016), 신장질환(p=0.044), 전신마취(p=0.001), 더 긴 수술 시간(p=0.007)과 유의하게 관련이 있었다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Clear guidelines for managing patients on antiplatelet (AP) or anticoagulant (AC) therapy undergoing oculoplastic surgery are lacking. | This study investigates bleeding risk factors and evaluates the effectiveness of a standardised bleeding risk assessment in extraocular surgery. | Associations between SQ scores and preoperative/demographic factors (AP/AC use, age, sex, comorbidities), and surgical factors (blood pressure, surgery type, primary vs revision surgery, anaesthesia type, duration, pain management) were assessed.

evidence.title: Benefits of pre-operative oral Sucrosomial® iron supplementation in cardiac surgery: influence of patient's baseline hemoglobin and gender.
evidence.authors: Weltert LP; De Rosa A; Rondinelli MB; Falco M; Turani F; Pierelli L
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: RESULTS: At hospital admission, Hb had increased 0.7 g/dL and 0.1 g/dL, for Iron and Control groups, respectively (p<0.001), with no gender-related differences, leading to a decrease in transfusion rate (30 vs 59%, respectively; p<0.001) and transfusion index (0.5 units/patient vs 1.2 units/pt, respectively; p<0.001).
evidence.dose: 13 g/d | 60 mg/d | 0.7 g/d | 0.1 g/d | 0.5 units | 1.2 units
evidence.outcome: Main end-point variables were increase in Hb from randomization to hospital admission, transfusion requirements, and cost-effectiveness of Sucrosomial® iron administration. | RESULTS: At hospital admission, Hb had increased 0.7 g/dL and 0.1 g/dL, for Iron and Control groups, respectively (p<0.001), with no gender-related differences, leading to a decrease in transfusion rate (30 vs 59%, respectively; p<0.001) and transfusion index (0.5 units/patient vs 1.2 units/pt, respectively; p<0.001). | CONCLUSIONS: This post-hoc analysis confirms pre-operative Sucrosomial® iron administration is a safe and cost-effective strategy to increase preoperative Hb and decrease transfusion requirements in elective cardiac surgery, especially in those anemic at baseline.
evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: At hospital admission, Hb had increased 0.7 g/dL and 0.1 g/dL, for Iron and Control groups, respectively (p<0.001), with no gender-related differences, leading to a decrease in transfusion rate (30 vs 59%, respectively; p<0.001) and transfusion index (0.5 units/patient vs 1.2 units/pt, respectively; p<0.001).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 입원 시 Hb는 철분군과 대조군에서 각각 0.7 g/dL와 0.1 g/dL 증가했으며(p<0.001), 성별에 따른 차이는 없었다. 이에 따라 수혈률(각각 30 vs 59%; p<0.001)과 수혈지수(각각 0.5 units/patient vs 1.2 units/pt; p<0.001)가 감소했다.
evidence.population: BACKGROUND: The prevalence of low pre-operative hemoglobin (Hb) among cardiac surgery patients is high. | Patients (pt) received a one-month course of 60 mg/day Sucrosomial® iron (Iron group, n=309) or routine care (Control group, n=285) prior to elective cardiac surgery. | CONCLUSIONS: This post-hoc analysis confirms pre-operative Sucrosomial® iron administration is a safe and cost-effective strategy to increase preoperative Hb and decrease transfusion requirements in elective cardiac surgery, especially in those anemic at baseline.

evidence.title: Fish Oil and Perioperative Bleeding.
evidence.authors: Akintoye E; Sethi P; Harris WS; Thompson PA; Marchioli R; Tavazzi L; Latini R; Pretorius M; Brown NJ; Libby P; Mozaffarian D
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_3: Methods and Results We tested the effect of fish oil supplementation on perioperative bleeding in a multinational, placebo-controlled trial involving 1516 patients who were randomized to perioperative fish oil (eicosapentaenoic acid+docosahexaenoic acid; 8-10 g for 2-5 days preoperatively, and then 2 g/d postoperatively) or placebo.
evidence.outcome: However, concerns about theoretical bleeding risk have led to recommendations that patients should stop taking fish oil before surgery or delay in elective procedures for patients taking fish oil by some health care professionals. | Methods and Results We tested the effect of fish oil supplementation on perioperative bleeding in a multinational, placebo-controlled trial involving 1516 patients who were randomized to perioperative fish oil (eicosapentaenoic acid+docosahexaenoic acid; 8-10 g for 2-5 days preoperatively, and then 2 g/d postoperatively) or placebo. | Primary outcome was major perioperative bleeding as defined by the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium.
evidence.key_finding: Methods and Results We tested the effect of fish oil supplementation on perioperative bleeding in a multinational, placebo-controlled trial involving 1516 patients who were randomized to perioperative fish oil (eicosapentaenoic acid+docosahexaenoic acid; 8-10 g for 2-5 days preoperatively, and then 2 g/d postoperatively) or placebo.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 방법 및 결과: 1516명의 환자가 참여한 다국가 위약 대조 시험에서 수술 전후 어유 보충이 출혈에 미치는 영향을 평가했다. 환자들은 수술 전후 어유(에이코사펜타엔산+도코사헥사엔산; 8-10 g을 수술 전 2-5일 동안, 이후 수술 후 2 g/d)군 또는 위약군에 무작위 배정되었다.
evidence.population: However, concerns about theoretical bleeding risk have led to recommendations that patients should stop taking fish oil before surgery or delay in elective procedures for patients taking fish oil by some health care professionals. | Methods and Results We tested the effect of fish oil supplementation on perioperative bleeding in a multinational, placebo-controlled trial involving 1516 patients who were randomized to perioperative fish oil (eicosapentaenoic acid+docosahexaenoic acid; 8-10 g for 2-5 days preoperatively, and then 2 g/d postoperatively) or placebo. | Primary outcome was major perioperative bleeding as defined by the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium.

evidence.title: Benefits of pre-operative oral Sucrosomial® iron supplementation in cardiac surgery: influence of patient's baseline hemoglobin and gender.

evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: RESULTS: At hospital admission, Hb had increased 0.7 g/dL and 0.1 g/dL, for Iron and Control groups, respectively (p<0.001), with no gender-related differences, leading to a decrease in transfusion rate (30 vs 59%, respectively; p<0.001) and transfusion index (0.5 units/patient vs 1.2 units/pt, respectively; p<0.001).

evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: At hospital admission, Hb had increased 0.7 g/dL and 0.1 g/dL, for Iron and Control groups, respectively (p<0.001), with no gender-related differences, leading to a decrease in transfusion rate (30 vs 59%, respectively; p<0.001) and transfusion index (0.5 units/patient vs 1.2 units/pt, respectively; p<0.001).

evidence.title: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Preoperative Antithrombin Supplementation in Patients at Risk for Antithrombin Deficiency After Cardiac Surgery.
evidence.authors: Moront MG; Woodward MK; Essandoh MK; Avery EG; Reece TB; Brzezinski M; Spiess B; Shore-Lesserson L; Chen J; Henriquez W; Barceló M; Despotis G; Karkouti K; Levy JH; Ranucci M; Mondou E; Clinical Thrombate Study Group
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_2: Preoperative AT supplementation, to achieve >58% and <100% AT activity, may potentially reduce postoperative morbidity and mortality in cardiac operations with CPB.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Antithrombin (AT) activity is reduced during cardiac operations with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), which is associated with adverse outcomes. | Preoperative AT supplementation, to achieve >58% and <100% AT activity, may potentially reduce postoperative morbidity and mortality in cardiac operations with CPB. | The primary efficacy end point was the percentage of patients with any component of a major morbidity composite (postoperative mortality, stroke, acute kidney injury [AKI], surgical reexploration, arterial or venous thromboembolic events, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and infection) in the 2 groups.

evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Multicenter Study|Randomized Controlled Trial|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
evidence.population: Preoperative AT supplementation, to achieve >58% and <100% AT activity, may potentially reduce postoperative morbidity and mortality in cardiac operations with CPB. | This prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study was designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of preoperative treatment with AT supplementation in patients at risk for low AT activity after undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. | METHODS: A total of 425 adult patients were randomized (1:1) to receive either a single dose of AT (n = 213) to achieve an absolute increase of 20% above pretreatment AT activity or placebo (n = 212) before surgery.

all_evidence.title: Risk factors for bleeding and perioperative bleeding complications in oculoplastic surgery: a prospective pilot study.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).

evidence.population: This systematic review aimed to collect the best available evidence on the effectiveness of preoperative iron supplementation with or without erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) on red blood cell (RBC) utilization in all-cause anaemic patients scheduled for elective surgery. | We identified 29 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 2 non-RCTs comparing the effectiveness of preoperative iron monotherapy, or iron + ESAs, to control (no treatment, usual care, placebo). | In conclusion, in patients with anaemia of any cause scheduled for elective surgery, the preoperative administration of iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of patients or units transfused (low-certainty evidence).

all_evidence.title: Benefits of pre-operative oral Sucrosomial® iron supplementation in cardiac surgery: influence of patient's baseline hemoglobin and gender.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: RESULTS: At hospital admission, Hb had increased 0.7 g/dL and 0.1 g/dL, for Iron and Control groups, respectively (p<0.001), with no gender-related differences, leading to a decrease in transfusion rate (30 vs 59%, respectively; p<0.001) and transfusion index (0.5 units/patient vs 1.2 units/pt, respectively; p<0.001).

all_evidence.title: Perioperative omega-3 fatty acids for liver surgery: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.authors: Xiao F; Han W; Yue Q; Ke J; Jia B; Fu X
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: Overall, compared with control group for liver surgery, omega-3 fatty acids were associated with substantially reduced incidence of infection (odd ratio [OR]=0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] =0.34-0.91; P = .02), but revealed no remarkable influence on complications (OR = 0.60; 95% CI = 0.29-1.24; P = .17), mortality (OR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.06-9.37; P = .83), liver failure (OR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.10 to 5.00; P = 0.74), biliary leakage (OR=1.24; 95% CI = 0.41 to 3.76; P = .70), bleeding (OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 0.63-4.95; P = .28), or ileus (OR = 0.39; 95% CI = 0.07-2.05; P = .27).

all_evidence.key_finding: METHODS: In a prospective, randomized placebo-controlled trial consisting of 95 patients, we compared the incidence of postoperative infections and other complications after liver transplantation among three different groups, all supplied with early enteral nutrition: (a) standard formula plus selective bowel decontamination (SBD), (b) fiber-containing formula plus living Lactobacillus plantarum 299, and (c) fiber-containing formula plus heat-killed L plantarum 299.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 방법: 95명의 환자로 구성된 전향적 무작위 위약 대조 시험에서 모든 군에 조기 경장영양을 제공하고 간 이식 후 수술 후 감염과 기타 합병증 발생률을 세 군 간 비교했다. 세 군은 (a) 표준 조제식 + 선택적 장 오염 제거(SBD), (b) 섬유 함유 조제식 + 살아 있는 Lactobacillus plantarum 299, (c) 섬유 함유 조제식 + 열처리로 사멸시킨 L plantarum 299였다.

all_evidence.title: Comprehensive preoperative regime of selective gut decontamination in combination with probiotics, and smectite for reducing endotoxemia and cytokine activation during cardiopulmonary bypass: A pilot randomized, controlled trial.
all_evidence.authors: Liu WC; Zhan YP; Wang XH; Hou BC; Huang J; Chen SB
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: RESULTS: The mean levels of change in endotoxin levels after CPB in patients receiving the comprehensive preoperative regimen was marginally significantly lower than those in control group (F = 4.0, P = .0552) but was not significantly different for procalcitonin (F = .14, P = .7134).
all_evidence.outcome: An interaction between group and time for IL-6 was identified (F = 4.35, P = .0231).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: The mean levels of change in endotoxin levels after CPB in patients receiving the comprehensive preoperative regimen was marginally significantly lower than those in control group (F = 4.0, P = .0552) but was not significantly different for procalcitonin (F = .14, P = .7134).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 종합 수술 전 처치를 받은 환자에서 CPB 후 엔도톡신 수치 변화의 평균은 대조군보다 유의성의 경계 수준으로 낮았지만(F = 4.0, P = .0552), 프로칼시토닌은 유의한 차이가 없었다(F = .14, P = .7134).
all_evidence.population: This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of a comprehensive preoperative regimen of SDD in combination with probiotics and smectite on perioperative endotoxemia and cytokine activation in patients who underwent elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) in a pilot, prospective, randomized, controlled trial. | METHODS: Patients who underwent elective Aortic Valve Replacement or Mitral Valve Replacement surgery from July 2010 to March 2015 were included. | In total, 30 eligible patients were randomly assigned to receive either the comprehensive preoperative regimen (n = 15) (a combination of preoperative SDD, probiotics, and smectite) or the control group (n = 15) who did not receive this treatment.

all_evidence.title: Preoperative Sucrosomial Iron Supplementation Increases Haemoglobin and Reduces Transfusion Requirements in Elective Heart Surgery Patients: A Prospective Randomized Study.
all_evidence.authors: Pierelli L; De Rosa A; Falco M; Papi E; Rondinelli MB; Turani F; Weltert L
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_15: CONCLUSION: In elective heart surgery, routine preoperative sucrosomial iron administration seems to be a safe, well-tolerated and cost-effective strategy to increase preoperative haemoglobin and reduce the need for allogeneic blood transfusions.
all_evidence.outcome: Overall, these patients tend to receive many RBC transfusions. | Primary end-points were haemoglobin concentration on the day of hospital admittance and number of blood transfusions. | The percentage of patients in the treatment group who required transfusion (35.4%) was half that in the control group (64.6%).
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSION: In elective heart surgery, routine preoperative sucrosomial iron administration seems to be a safe, well-tolerated and cost-effective strategy to increase preoperative haemoglobin and reduce the need for allogeneic blood transfusions.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 결론: 선택적 심장 수술에서 수술 전 수크로소미얼 철분의 일상적 투여는 수술 전 헤모글로빈을 높이고 동종 혈액 수혈 필요성을 줄이는 안전하고 내약성이 좋으며 비용 효과적인 전략으로 보인다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Low preoperative haemoglobin is frequently observed in heart surgery patients and is associated with a significant decrease in haemoglobin between post-operative days 2 and 3, known as haemoglobin drift. | STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: The purpose of this study was to assess whether preoperative supplementation with oral sucrosomial iron, a new iron-delivery technology with improved tolerance and bioavailability, might be an effective strategy for this patient population. | One thousand consecutive patients were randomized and received either a one-month course of sucrosomial iron (60 mg/day) or no treatment prior to elective heart surgery at a single high-volume centre (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03560687).

all_evidence.title: Effects of omega-3 fatty acids supplementation on perioperative blood loss and complications after radical prostatectomy.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: RESULTS: We found no clinically significant effect of LCω3 versus placebo on perioperative bleeding, laboratory tests or postoperative complications.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Many dietary supplements, including omega-3 fatty acids (ω3), are suspected to affect blood coagulation and platelet function. | Here, we aim to determine the effect of LCω3 supplements on perioperative bleeding, hemoglobin, platelets, and postoperative complications after radical prostatectomy. | An intention-to-treat analysis approach was used with bi-variate statistical testing of bleeding and complications outcomes.
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: We found no clinically significant effect of LCω3 versus placebo on perioperative bleeding, laboratory tests or postoperative complications.

all_evidence.title: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Preoperative Antithrombin Supplementation in Patients at Risk for Antithrombin Deficiency After Cardiac Surgery.
all_evidence.authors: Moront MG; Woodward MK; Essandoh MK; Avery EG; Reece TB; Brzezinski M; Spiess B; Shore-Lesserson L; Chen J; Henriquez W; Barceló M; Despotis G; Karkouti K; Levy JH; Ranucci M; Mondou E; Clinical Thrombate Study Group
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_2: Preoperative AT supplementation, to achieve >58% and <100% AT activity, may potentially reduce postoperative morbidity and mortality in cardiac operations with CPB.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Antithrombin (AT) activity is reduced during cardiac operations with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), which is associated with adverse outcomes. | Preoperative AT supplementation, to achieve >58% and <100% AT activity, may potentially reduce postoperative morbidity and mortality in cardiac operations with CPB. | The primary efficacy end point was the percentage of patients with any component of a major morbidity composite (postoperative mortality, stroke, acute kidney injury [AKI], surgical reexploration, arterial or venous thromboembolic events, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and infection) in the 2 groups.
all_evidence.key_finding: Preoperative AT supplementation, to achieve >58% and <100% AT activity, may potentially reduce postoperative morbidity and mortality in cardiac operations with CPB.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: AT 활성을 >58% 및 <100%로 달성하기 위한 수술 전 AT 보충은 CPB를 사용하는 심장 수술에서 수술 후 이환율과 사망률을 낮출 가능성이 있다.
all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Multicenter Study|Randomized Controlled Trial|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
all_evidence.population: Preoperative AT supplementation, to achieve >58% and <100% AT activity, may potentially reduce postoperative morbidity and mortality in cardiac operations with CPB. | This prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study was designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of preoperative treatment with AT supplementation in patients at risk for low AT activity after undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. | METHODS: A total of 425 adult patients were randomized (1:1) to receive either a single dose of AT (n = 213) to achieve an absolute increase of 20% above pretreatment AT activity or placebo (n = 212) before surgery.

all_evidence.title: Risk factors for bleeding and perioperative bleeding complications in oculoplastic surgery: a prospective pilot study.
all_evidence.authors: Christensen NA; Feltgen N; Horn M; Naxer S; van Oterendorp C; Koscielny J; Sucker C; Pfeiffer S; Kück F; Schittkowski MP
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Clear guidelines for managing patients on antiplatelet (AP) or anticoagulant (AC) therapy undergoing oculoplastic surgery are lacking. | This study investigates bleeding risk factors and evaluates the effectiveness of a standardised bleeding risk assessment in extraocular surgery. | METHODS: In this prospective study, a standardised questionnaire (SQ) was employed to gather patients' bleeding histories.
all_evidence.key_finding: Bleeding complications were significantly associated with higher SQ scores (p=0.048), acetylsalicylic acid use in eyelid surgery (p=0.038), diabetes mellitus (p=0.016), renal disease (p=0.044), general anaesthesia (p=0.001) and longer surgery duration (p=0.007).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 출혈 합병증은 더 높은 SQ 점수(p=0.048), 눈꺼풀 수술에서의 아세틸살리실산 사용(p=0.038), 당뇨병(p=0.016), 신장질환(p=0.044), 전신마취(p=0.001), 더 긴 수술 시간(p=0.007)과 유의하게 관련이 있었다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Clear guidelines for managing patients on antiplatelet (AP) or anticoagulant (AC) therapy undergoing oculoplastic surgery are lacking. | This study investigates bleeding risk factors and evaluates the effectiveness of a standardised bleeding risk assessment in extraocular surgery. | Associations between SQ scores and preoperative/demographic factors (AP/AC use, age, sex, comorbidities), and surgical factors (blood pressure, surgery type, primary vs revision surgery, anaesthesia type, duration, pain management) were assessed.

all_evidence.key_finding: Conclusions: Avoiding large variations in serum bicarbonate levels is an important step in hemodialysis patients' management because wide acidosis-alkalosis variation can increase cardiovascular risks in terms of altering the vessel walls elasticity and favoring their calcifications.

all_evidence.authors: Lu Y; Jiang G
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: There was no significant difference in the overall incidence of adverse events between the 2 groups (P > .05), and no serious adverse events occurred in either group.
all_evidence.outcome: Patients were followed for 8 weeks to evaluate hemoglobin (Hb) levels, iron metabolism parameters, erythropoietic parameters, and adverse events. | There was no significant difference in the overall incidence of adverse events between the 2 groups (P > .05), and no serious adverse events occurred in either group.
all_evidence.key_finding: There was no significant difference in the overall incidence of adverse events between the 2 groups (P > .05), and no serious adverse events occurred in either group.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 2개 군 간 전체 이상사례 발생률에는 유의한 차이가 없었고(P > .05), 두 군 모두에서 중대한 이상사례가 발생하지 않았다.
all_evidence.population: This study aimed to evaluate the synergistic effect and safety of enarodustat combined with oral iron supplementation in the treatment of iron-deficient non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease (NDD-CKD) patients with anemia. | This single-center retrospective cohort study enrolled 120 iron-deficient NDD-CKD patients with anemia who had not received erythropoiesis-stimulating agents or intravenous iron within the preceding month. | This study indicates that enarodustat combined with oral iron supplementation may have a certain synergistic effect on iron-deficient NDD-CKD anemia compared with oral iron alone, potentially helping to improve hematological indicators and promote erythropoiesis, with an acceptable safety profile.

all_evidence.title: Effects of Short-Term Potassium Chloride Supplementation in Patients with CKD.
all_evidence.authors: Gritter M; Wouda RD; Yeung SMH; Wieërs MLA; Geurts F; de Ridder MAJ; Ramakers CRB; Vogt L; de Borst MH; Rotmans JI; Hoorn EJ; on behalf of K onsortium
all_evidence.venue: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_1: BACKGROUND: Observational studies suggest that adequate dietary potassium intake (90-120 mmol/day) may be renoprotective, but the effects of increasing dietary potassium and the risk of hyperkalemia are unknown.
all_evidence.dose: 90-120 mmol/d | 9 ml | 40 mmol | 29 mmol/d | 0.6 mmol | 4 mmol | 3.5 mmol | 0.4 mmol
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Observational studies suggest that adequate dietary potassium intake (90-120 mmol/day) may be renoprotective, but the effects of increasing dietary potassium and the risk of hyperkalemia are unknown. | In total, 21 participants (11%) developed hyperkalemia (plasma potassium 5.9±0.4 mmol/L). | This may result in hyperkalemia in older patients or those with higher baseline plasma potassium.
all_evidence.key_finding: BACKGROUND: Observational studies suggest that adequate dietary potassium intake (90-120 mmol/day) may be renoprotective, but the effects of increasing dietary potassium and the risk of hyperkalemia are unknown.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 배경: 관찰 연구에 따르면 식이 칼륨을 적절히 섭취하면(90-120 mmol/day) 신장 보호 효과가 있을 수 있지만, 식이 칼륨 섭취를 늘리는 효과와 고칼륨혈증 위험은 알려져 있지 않다.
all_evidence.population: CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CKD stage G3b-4, increasing dietary potassium intake to recommended levels with potassium chloride supplementation raises plasma potassium by 0.4 mmol/L. | Longer-term studies should address whether cardiorenal protection outweighs the risk of hyperkalemia.Clinical trial number: NCT03253172.

all_evidence.title: Effects of low protein diet supplemented with ketoanalogues on kidney function and nutritional outcomes in a nonagenarian population with advanced chronic kidney disease: a pilot study.
all_evidence.authors: Annunziata G; Marinelli T; Melfitano A; Aucella F; Nardella M; Camajani E; Muscogiuri G; Caprio M; Aucella F; Barrea L
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: RESULTS: Significant change in GFR (from 18.04±1.31 to 24.30±2.09 mL/min, P<0.001), azotemia (from 122.38±19.16 to 70.19±15.00 mg/dL, P<0.001) and KFRE score at 2 years (from 33.67±3.88 to 15.09±3.03%, P<0.001) and at 5 years (from 71.94±5.13 to 39.76±6.60% at 5 years, P<0.001).
all_evidence.outcome: Two patients were hospitalized during the observation period, no cardiovascular events or deaths were reported.
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: Significant change in GFR (from 18.04±1.31 to 24.30±2.09 mL/min, P<0.001), azotemia (from 122.38±19.16 to 70.19±15.00 mg/dL, P<0.001) and KFRE score at 2 years (from 33.67±3.88 to 15.09±3.03%, P<0.001) and at 5 years (from 71.94±5.13 to 39.76±6.60% at 5 years, P<0.001).
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Ageing leads to an increase in the incidence of chronic diseases, including chronic kidney disease (CKD). | The increasing proportion of elderly people with reduced renal function draws attention to a sub-population of patients for whom an alternative approach to traditional pharmacological and dietary treatment may be needed. | The low-protein diet (LPD) in subjects with CKD helps control complications and may contribute to slowing the progression of the disease.

all_evidence.title: Nontraditional (non-Western pharmaceutical) treatments for chronic kidney disease.
all_evidence.authors: Gobe GC; Wojcikowski K
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_3: This review presents information on the treatment of kidney disease with CAM, particularly CKD and its closely associated cardiovascular disease (CVD), which might benefit vulnerable populations.
all_evidence.outcome: This review presents information on the treatment of kidney disease with CAM, particularly CKD and its closely associated cardiovascular disease (CVD), which might benefit vulnerable populations. | Also needing consideration are the recorded instances of nephrotoxicity from CAM therapies, particularly related to nephrotoxic plant extracts, extract-drug reactions, and toxicity from contaminants within the extracts. | As long as the possible toxicity of plant-derived CAM is considered, we argue that populations having marked deficiency in, or poor access to, dietary antioxidants, or high exposure to environmental oxidants, may benefit from these nontraditional medicines.
all_evidence.key_finding: This review presents information on the treatment of kidney disease with CAM, particularly CKD and its closely associated cardiovascular disease (CVD), which might benefit vulnerable populations.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 이 문헌고찰은 보완대체의학(CAM)을 이용한 신장질환 치료, 특히 CKD와 밀접하게 연관된 심혈관질환(CVD) 치료에 관한 정보를 제시하며, 이러한 치료는 취약 집단에 도움이 될 수 있다.
all_evidence.population: Nontraditional, non-Western medicines, often called complementary and alternative medicines (CAM), for chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients are, potentially, a huge low-cost therapy resource for poorer populations in the world. | This review presents information on the treatment of kidney disease with CAM, particularly CKD and its closely associated cardiovascular disease (CVD), which might benefit vulnerable populations. | The challenges of developing CAM therapies for resource-limited environments are also discussed, particularly with reference to targeting oxidative stress, a known cause of progressive diseases such as CKD and CVD.

all_evidence.title: Fanconi syndrome with acute proximal tubular injury induced by a dietary supplement containing beni-koji: a case series report.
all_evidence.authors: Habuka M; Hosojima M; Yata Y; Kurumada K; Yamagiwa M; Yonezawa M; Sudo M; Kabasawa H; Ogawa A; Hama H; Ito Y; Imai N; Yamamoto S; Saito A; Goto S
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_1: BACKGROUND: Fanconi syndrome is a disorder of the proximal tubule that leads to malabsorption of various electrolytes and substances and is a common consequence of drug-induced nephrotoxicity.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Fanconi syndrome is a disorder of the proximal tubule that leads to malabsorption of various electrolytes and substances and is a common consequence of drug-induced nephrotoxicity. | After discontinuation of the dietary supplement and correction of dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, renal function completely recovered in one case but progressed to chronic kidney disease in the other.
all_evidence.key_finding: BACKGROUND: Fanconi syndrome is a disorder of the proximal tubule that leads to malabsorption of various electrolytes and substances and is a common consequence of drug-induced nephrotoxicity.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 배경: 판코니 증후군은 다양한 전해질과 물질의 재흡수 장애를 일으키는 근위세뇨관 질환이며, 약물 유발 신독성의 흔한 결과이다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Fanconi syndrome is a disorder of the proximal tubule that leads to malabsorption of various electrolytes and substances and is a common consequence of drug-induced nephrotoxicity. | However, cases of dietary supplement-induced Fanconi syndrome are rare, and detailed reports on the evaluation of renal histology in patients with this syndrome are lacking. | CASE PRESENTATION: We present two cases of dietary supplement-induced Fanconi syndrome that was confirmed by kidney biopsy.

evidence.title: Herbal Medicinal Product Use During Pregnancy and the Postnatal Period: A Systematic Review.
evidence.authors: Muñoz Balbontín Y; Stewart D; Shetty A; Fitton CA; McLay JS
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Adverse drug reactions, congenital malformations, fetal growth retardation or herb-drug interactions were the primary study objective reported by 19 of the 74 included studies, 16 cohort studies, one cross-sectional survey, and two randomized controlled trials.
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: To report the incidence and nature of herbal medicinal products' adverse events and herb-drug interactions used by some pregnant and postnatal women. | DATA SOURCES: The Allied and Complementary Medicine Database, the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception until August 2018. | METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Any studies reporting adverse events, herb-drug interactions or absence thereof associated with herbal medicinal products used during pregnancy or the postnatal period were included.
evidence.key_finding: Adverse drug reactions, congenital malformations, fetal growth retardation or herb-drug interactions were the primary study objective reported by 19 of the 74 included studies, 16 cohort studies, one cross-sectional survey, and two randomized controlled trials.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 약물 이상반응, 선천성 기형, 태아 성장 지연 또는 허브-약물 상호작용은 포함된 74편의 연구 중 19편(코호트 연구 16편, 횡단면 조사 한 편, 무작위 대조시험 두 편)이 보고한 주요 연구 목적이었다.
evidence.population: OBJECTIVE: To report the incidence and nature of herbal medicinal products' adverse events and herb-drug interactions used by some pregnant and postnatal women. | METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Any studies reporting adverse events, herb-drug interactions or absence thereof associated with herbal medicinal products used during pregnancy or the postnatal period were included. | Adverse drug reactions, congenital malformations, fetal growth retardation or herb-drug interactions were the primary study objective reported by 19 of the 74 included studies, 16 cohort studies, one cross-sectional survey, and two randomized controlled trials.

evidence.title: The effects of progesterone supplementation in pregnancies assessed by doppler ultrasound: a systematic review of maternal and perinatal outcomes.
evidence.authors: Khanjani S; Goodarzi SB; Khaleghi MM; Moosavi SSA; Eshraghi R; Meigoli MS; Fathi M; Azadani MN; Sadraei N; Bahrami A
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_12: CONCLUSIONS: Progesterone supplementation in early and mid-pregnancy may benefit certain subgroups, particularly those at risk of preterm birth.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Progesterone is essential for pregnancy maintenance, but its effects on complications like intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), preeclampsia, prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM), preterm birth, and placental abruption are still debated. | MATERIAL AND METHODS: To assess the efficacy of progesterone supplements in reducing pregnancy complications during the first and second trimesters using Doppler ultrasound indices. | The primary outcomes were Doppler ultrasound indices, with secondary outcomes including preterm birth, IUGR, preeclampsia, PROM, and placental abruption.
evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: Progesterone supplementation in early and mid-pregnancy may benefit certain subgroups, particularly those at risk of preterm birth.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 결론: 임신 초기와 중기의 프로게스테론 보충은 특정 하위 집단, 특히 조산 위험이 있는 사람들에게 도움이 될 수 있다.
evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Progesterone is essential for pregnancy maintenance, but its effects on complications like intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), preeclampsia, prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM), preterm birth, and placental abruption are still debated. | This review investigates the effects of progesterone supplementation on Doppler ultrasound indices and pregnancy outcomes. | MATERIAL AND METHODS: To assess the efficacy of progesterone supplements in reducing pregnancy complications during the first and second trimesters using Doppler ultrasound indices.

evidence.title: Vitamin D deficiency in pregnant women: obstetric implications and clinical management.
evidence.authors: Tadros-Zins M; Krekora M; Zych-Krekora K; Drosdzol-Cop A
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: This review analyzes current evidence regarding vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy from an obstetric perspective, focusing on pregnancy complications, fetal outcomes, and evidence-based supplementation strategies for clinical practice. | RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 분석 결과, 비타민 D 결핍(< 50 nmol/L)과 자간전증(OR 0.65), 임신성 당뇨병(OR 1.61), 조산(RR 0.67), 재태연령 대비 저체중 신생아(RR 0.61)의 위험 증가 사이에 유의한 연관성이 확인되었다.
evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Vitamin D deficiency in pregnant women constitutes a significant obstetric concern, affecting 40-98% of gravid populations worldwide. | Adequate vitamin D status is essential for successful pregnancy outcomes, fetal development, and maternal health. | OBJECTIVE: This review analyzes current evidence regarding vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy from an obstetric perspective, focusing on pregnancy complications, fetal outcomes, and evidence-based supplementation strategies for clinical practice.

all_evidence.title: Vitamin C supplementation in pregnancy.
all_evidence.authors: Rumbold A; Ota E; Nagata C; Shahrook S; Crowther CA
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: No clear differences were seen between women supplemented with vitamin C alone or in combination with other supplements compared with placebo or no control for the risk of stillbirth (risk ratio (RR) 1.15, 95% confidence intervals (CI) 0.89 to 1.49; 20,038 participants; 11 studies; I² = 0%; moderate quality evidence), neonatal death (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.08; 19,575 participants; 11 studies; I² = 0%), perinatal death (average RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.49; 17,105 participants; seven studies; I² = 35%), birthweight (mean difference (MD) 26.88 g, 95% CI -18.81 to 72.58; 17,326 participants; 13 studies; I² = 69%), intrauterine growth restriction (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.06; 20,361 participants; 12 studies; I² = 15%; high quality evidence), preterm birth (average RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.10; 22,250 participants; 16 studies; I² = 49%; high quality evidence), preterm PROM (prelabour rupture of membranes) (average RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.36; 16,825 participants; 10 studies; I² = 70%; low quality evidence), term PROM (average RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.62 to 2.56; 2674 participants; three studies; I² = 87%), and clinical pre-eclampsia (average RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.05; 21,956 participants; 16 studies; I² = 41%; high quality evidence).Women supplemented with vitamin C alone or in combination with other supplements compared with placebo or no control were at decreased risk of having a placental abruption (RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.92; 15,755 participants; eight studies; I² = 0%; high quality evidence) and had a small increase in gestational age at birth (MD 0.31, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.61; 14,062 participants; nine studies; I² = 65%), however they were also more likely to self-report abdominal pain (RR 1.66, 95% CI 1.16 to 2.37; 1877 participants; one study).

all_evidence.key_finding: No clear differences were seen between women supplemented with vitamin C alone or in combination with other supplements compared with placebo or no control for the risk of stillbirth (risk ratio (RR) 1.15, 95% confidence intervals (CI) 0.89 to 1.49; 20,038 participants; 11 studies; I² = 0%; moderate quality evidence), neonatal death (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.08; 19,575 participants; 11 studies; I² = 0%), perinatal death (average RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.49; 17,105 participants; seven studies; I² = 35%), birthweight (mean difference (MD) 26.88 g, 95% CI -18.81 to 72.58; 17,326 participants; 13 studies; I² = 69%), intrauterine growth restriction (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.06; 20,361 participants; 12 studies; I² = 15%; high quality evidence), preterm birth (average RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.10; 22,250 participants; 16 studies; I² = 49%; high quality evidence), preterm PROM (prelabour rupture of membranes) (average RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.36; 16,825 participants; 10 studies; I² = 70%; low quality evidence), term PROM (average RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.62 to 2.56; 2674 participants; three studies; I² = 87%), and clinical pre-eclampsia (average RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.05; 21,956 participants; 16 studies; I² = 41%; high quality evidence).Women supplemented with vitamin C alone or in combination with other supplements compared with placebo or no control were at decreased risk of having a placental abruption (RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.92; 15,755 participants; eight studies; I² = 0%; high quality evidence) and had a small increase in gestational age at birth (MD 0.31, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.61; 14,062 participants; nine studies; I² = 65%), however they were also more likely to self-report abdominal pain (RR 1.66, 95% CI 1.16 to 2.37; 1877 participants; one study).

all_evidence.title: Intermittent oral iron supplementation during pregnancy.

all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.outcome: None of the studies reported congenital anomalies.For maternal outcomes, there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for anaemia at term (average RR 1.22; 95% CI 0.84 to 1.80; participants = 676; studies = four; I² = 10%; very low quality). | There were no clear differences between groups for mean birthweight, preterm birth, maternal anaemia or maternal side effects.

all_evidence.key_finding: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: This review analyzes current evidence regarding vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy from an obstetric perspective, focusing on pregnancy complications, fetal outcomes, and evidence-based supplementation strategies for clinical practice. | RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).

all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Vitamin D deficiency in pregnant women constitutes a significant obstetric concern, affecting 40-98% of gravid populations worldwide. | Adequate vitamin D status is essential for successful pregnancy outcomes, fetal development, and maternal health. | OBJECTIVE: This review analyzes current evidence regarding vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy from an obstetric perspective, focusing on pregnancy complications, fetal outcomes, and evidence-based supplementation strategies for clinical practice.
