all_evidence.title: Intermittent oral iron supplementation during pregnancy.
all_evidence.authors: Peña-Rosas JP; De-Regil LM; Gomez Malave H; Flores-Urrutia MC; Dowswell T
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.outcome: None of the studies reported congenital anomalies.For maternal outcomes, there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for anaemia at term (average RR 1.22; 95% CI 0.84 to 1.80; participants = 676; studies = four; I² = 10%; very low quality). | There were no clear differences between groups for mean birthweight, preterm birth, maternal anaemia or maternal side effects.
all_evidence.key_finding: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 포함된 연구의 방법론적 질은 일관되지 않았고, 대부분 탈락률이 높았다. 주요 영아 결과에 관한 근거의 전반적 질은 낮았으며, 산모 결과에 관한 근거의 질은 매우 낮았다. 자료를 제공한 21개 시험 중 세 연구는 간헐적 철분 단독 요법, 14개 연구는 간헐적 철분 + 엽산 요법, 네 연구는 간헐적 철분과 복합 비타민·미네랄 요법을 각각 동일 조성의 일일 보충 요법과 비교했다. 전체적으로 간헐적 철분 요법(다른 비타민과 미네랄의 병용 여부 무관)을 받은 여성과 일일 요법을 받은 여성을 비교했을 때, 저체중 출생(평균 위험비(RR) 0.82; 95% 신뢰구간(CI) 0.55 to 1.22; 참여자 = 1898명; 연구 = 여덟 개; 낮은 질 근거), 영아 출생체중(평균차(MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; 참여자 = 1939명; 연구 = 아홉 개; 낮은 질 근거), 조산(평균 RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; 참여자 = 1177명; 연구 = 다섯 개; 낮은 질 근거), 신생아 사망(평균 RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; 참여자 = 795명; 연구 = 한 개; 매우 낮은 질 근거) 등 어떤 주요 영아 결과에서도 집단 간 차이에 대한 명확한 근거가 없었다.

all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Anaemia is a frequent condition during pregnancy, particularly among women in low- and middle-income countries. | Traditionally, gestational anaemia has been prevented with daily iron supplements throughout pregnancy, but adherence to this regimen due to side effects, interrupted supply of the supplements, and concerns about safety among women with an adequate iron intake, have limited the use of this intervention. | OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of intermittent supplementation with iron alone or in combination with folic acid or other vitamins and minerals to pregnant women on neonatal and pregnancy outcomes.

all_evidence.title: The effects of oral ferrous bisglycinate supplementation on hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations in adults and children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.authors: Fischer JAJ; Cherian AM; Bone JN; Karakochuk CD
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).
all_evidence.outcome: Iron salts are commonly provided as oral supplements to prevent and treat iron deficiency, despite poor bioavailability and frequently reported adverse side effects. | Ferrous bisglycinate is a novel amino acid iron chelate that is thought to be more bioavailable and associated with fewer gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events as compared with iron salts. | OBJECTIVE: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted to evaluate the effects of ferrous bisglycinate supplementation compared with other iron supplements on hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations and GI adverse events.
all_evidence.key_finding: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 자료 분석: 다른 철분 보충제와 비교했을 때, 4-20주 동안 철 비스글리시네이트를 보충한 임신부는 헤모글로빈 농도가 더 높았고(SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% 신뢰구간[CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01), 보고된 위장관 이상반응은 더 적었다(IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_5: Since 1998, mandatory fortification of certain foods with folate has been associated with at least a 54% reduction in the incidence of open neural tube defects, yet rates of periconceptional folic acid use remain suboptimal, especially in minority women.
all_evidence.outcome: Furthermore, a reduction in the incidence of congenital cardiac and urologic anomalies has been demonstrated in some studies following periconceptional folic acid supplementation. | There is growing evidence of a possible role of folic acid supplementation in the prevention of other congenital anomalies, including cardiac defects.

all_evidence.population: Since 1992, a number of national and international professional societies have released guidelines recommending folic acid supplementation of at least 0.4 mg/day for all women of childbearing age or women planning pregnancies, and 4 mg/day for women with a previous infant with a neural tube defect.

all_evidence.title: Vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy.

all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy may help improve maternal and neonatal health outcomes (such as fewer preterm birth and low birthweight babies) and reduce the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes (such as severe postpartum haemorrhage). | The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of supplementation with vitamin D during pregnancy compared to placebo or no intervention on pre-eclampsia (risk ratio (RR) 0.53, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.21 to 1.33; 1 study, 165 women), gestational diabetes (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.03 to 8.28; 1 study, 165 women), preterm birth (< 37 weeks) (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.25 to 2.33; 3 studies, 1368 women), nephritic syndrome (RR 0.17, 95% CI 0.01 to 4.06; 1 study, 135 women), or hypercalcaemia (1 study; no cases reported). | Pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, and maternal adverse events were not reported.

evidence.title: Herbal Medicinal Product Use During Pregnancy and the Postnatal Period: A Systematic Review.
evidence.authors: Muñoz Balbontín Y; Stewart D; Shetty A; Fitton CA; McLay JS
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Adverse drug reactions, congenital malformations, fetal growth retardation or herb-drug interactions were the primary study objective reported by 19 of the 74 included studies, 16 cohort studies, one cross-sectional survey, and two randomized controlled trials.
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: To report the incidence and nature of herbal medicinal products' adverse events and herb-drug interactions used by some pregnant and postnatal women. | DATA SOURCES: The Allied and Complementary Medicine Database, the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception until August 2018. | METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Any studies reporting adverse events, herb-drug interactions or absence thereof associated with herbal medicinal products used during pregnancy or the postnatal period were included.
evidence.key_finding: Adverse drug reactions, congenital malformations, fetal growth retardation or herb-drug interactions were the primary study objective reported by 19 of the 74 included studies, 16 cohort studies, one cross-sectional survey, and two randomized controlled trials.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 약물 이상반응, 선천성 기형, 태아 성장 지연 또는 허브-약물 상호작용은 포함된 74편의 연구 중 19편(코호트 연구 16편, 횡단면 조사 한 편, 무작위 대조시험 두 편)이 보고한 주요 연구 목적이었다.

evidence.title: Effect of ginger in the treatment of nausea and vomiting compared with vitamin B6 and placebo during pregnancy: a meta-analysis.
evidence.authors: Hu Y; Amoah AN; Zhang H; Fu R; Qiu Y; Cao Y; Sun Y; Chen H; Liu Y; Lyu Q
evidence.venue: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: The result demonstrated that ginger intervention has significant effect in improving general symptom of NVP [OR = 7.475, 95% CI = (4.133, 13.520), I2 = 30.1%], relieving severity of nausea [SMD = 0.821, 95% CI = (0.585, 1.056), I2 = 38.9%], but not significant in reducing vomiting [SMD = 0.549, 95% CI = (-0.268, 1.365), I2 = 91.4%], compared with placebo.
evidence.outcome: Considering the potential teratogenic effect in fetus due to chemical drugs, ginger can be used to treat nausea and vomiting during pregnancy.
evidence.key_finding: The result demonstrated that ginger intervention has significant effect in improving general symptom of NVP [OR = 7.475, 95% CI = (4.133, 13.520), I2 = 30.1%], relieving severity of nausea [SMD = 0.821, 95% CI = (0.585, 1.056), I2 = 38.9%], but not significant in reducing vomiting [SMD = 0.549, 95% CI = (-0.268, 1.365), I2 = 91.4%], compared with placebo.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 위약과 비교했을 때 생강 중재는 임신 중 오심·구토(NVP)의 전반적 증상 개선에 유의한 효과가 있었고[OR = 7.475, 95% CI = (4.133, 13.520), I2 = 30.1%], 오심의 중증도를 완화했지만[SMD = 0.821, 95% CI = (0.585, 1.056), I2 = 38.9%], 구토 감소 효과는 유의하지 않았다[SMD = 0.549, 95% CI = (-0.268, 1.365), I2 = 91.4%].
evidence.population: INTRODUCTION: Nausea and vomiting (NV) affect up to 85% of pregnant women, which has multiple effects on pregnancy outcome. | The truth etiology of nausea and vomiting in pregnancy (NVP) is still unknown. | Considering the potential teratogenic effect in fetus due to chemical drugs, ginger can be used to treat nausea and vomiting during pregnancy.

evidence.title: Potential benefits versus hazards of herbal therapy during pregnancy; a systematic review of available literature.
evidence.authors: Balarastaghi S; Delirrad M; Jafari A; Majidi M; Sadeghi M; Zare-Zardini H; Karimi G; Ghorani-Azam A
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: From 35 articles with a total of 39,950 study population, the results showed that some medicinal plants could cause severe toxicity on mothers and fetuses, in addition to abortion during pregnancy.
evidence.outcome: Many clinical reports have shown that some herbal medicines may have toxic effects on pregnant women and their fetuses because active ingredients of some medicinal plants can readily pass through the biological barriers (e.g., placental barrier). | In the present study, we aimed to systematically review the literature to discover potential benefits versus the hazards of herbal therapy during pregnancy. | For this purpose, a comprehensive literature review was performed, and after the literature search and selection of the appropriate documents, the desired data were extracted and reported.
evidence.key_finding: From 35 articles with a total of 39,950 study population, the results showed that some medicinal plants could cause severe toxicity on mothers and fetuses, in addition to abortion during pregnancy.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 총 39,950명의 연구 대상자를 포함한 35편의 논문을 검토한 결과, 일부 약용 식물은 임신 중 유산을 일으킬 수 있을 뿐 아니라 산모와 태아에게 심각한 독성을 유발할 수 있었다.
evidence.population: Studies have shown that the prevalence of herbal diet therapy in pregnancy ranged from 1% to 60% in different societies. | Many clinical reports have shown that some herbal medicines may have toxic effects on pregnant women and their fetuses because active ingredients of some medicinal plants can readily pass through the biological barriers (e.g., placental barrier). | In the present study, we aimed to systematically review the literature to discover potential benefits versus the hazards of herbal therapy during pregnancy.

evidence.authors: Tadros-Zins M; Krekora M; Zych-Krekora K; Drosdzol-Cop A
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: This review analyzes current evidence regarding vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy from an obstetric perspective, focusing on pregnancy complications, fetal outcomes, and evidence-based supplementation strategies for clinical practice. | RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 분석 결과, 비타민 D 결핍(< 50 nmol/L)과 자간전증(OR 0.65), 임신성 당뇨병(OR 1.61), 조산(RR 0.67), 재태연령 대비 저체중 신생아(RR 0.61)의 위험 증가 사이에 유의한 연관성이 확인되었다.
evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Vitamin D deficiency in pregnant women constitutes a significant obstetric concern, affecting 40-98% of gravid populations worldwide. | Adequate vitamin D status is essential for successful pregnancy outcomes, fetal development, and maternal health. | OBJECTIVE: This review analyzes current evidence regarding vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy from an obstetric perspective, focusing on pregnancy complications, fetal outcomes, and evidence-based supplementation strategies for clinical practice.

evidence.title: Vitamin C supplementation in pregnancy.
evidence.authors: Rumbold A; Ota E; Nagata C; Shahrook S; Crowther CA
evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: No clear differences were seen between women supplemented with vitamin C alone or in combination with other supplements compared with placebo or no control for the risk of stillbirth (risk ratio (RR) 1.15, 95% confidence intervals (CI) 0.89 to 1.49; 20,038 participants; 11 studies; I² = 0%; moderate quality evidence), neonatal death (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.08; 19,575 participants; 11 studies; I² = 0%), perinatal death (average RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.49; 17,105 participants; seven studies; I² = 35%), birthweight (mean difference (MD) 26.88 g, 95% CI -18.81 to 72.58; 17,326 participants; 13 studies; I² = 69%), intrauterine growth restriction (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.06; 20,361 participants; 12 studies; I² = 15%; high quality evidence), preterm birth (average RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.10; 22,250 participants; 16 studies; I² = 49%; high quality evidence), preterm PROM (prelabour rupture of membranes) (average RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.36; 16,825 participants; 10 studies; I² = 70%; low quality evidence), term PROM (average RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.62 to 2.56; 2674 participants; three studies; I² = 87%), and clinical pre-eclampsia (average RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.05; 21,956 participants; 16 studies; I² = 41%; high quality evidence).Women supplemented with vitamin C alone or in combination with other supplements compared with placebo or no control were at decreased risk of having a placental abruption (RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.92; 15,755 participants; eight studies; I² = 0%; high quality evidence) and had a small increase in gestational age at birth (MD 0.31, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.61; 14,062 participants; nine studies; I² = 65%), however they were also more likely to self-report abdominal pain (RR 1.66, 95% CI 1.16 to 2.37; 1877 participants; one study).

evidence.title: Intermittent oral iron supplementation during pregnancy.
evidence.authors: Peña-Rosas JP; De-Regil LM; Gomez Malave H; Flores-Urrutia MC; Dowswell T
evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
evidence.outcome: None of the studies reported congenital anomalies.For maternal outcomes, there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for anaemia at term (average RR 1.22; 95% CI 0.84 to 1.80; participants = 676; studies = four; I² = 10%; very low quality). | There were no clear differences between groups for mean birthweight, preterm birth, maternal anaemia or maternal side effects.
evidence.key_finding: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 포함된 연구의 방법론적 질은 일관되지 않았고, 대부분 탈락률이 높았다. 주요 영아 결과에 관한 근거의 전반적 질은 낮았으며, 산모 결과에 관한 근거의 질은 매우 낮았다. 자료를 제공한 21개 시험 중 세 연구는 간헐적 철분 단독 요법, 14개 연구는 간헐적 철분 + 엽산 요법, 네 연구는 간헐적 철분과 복합 비타민·미네랄 요법을 각각 동일 조성의 일일 보충 요법과 비교했다. 전체적으로 간헐적 철분 요법(다른 비타민과 미네랄의 병용 여부 무관)을 받은 여성과 일일 요법을 받은 여성을 비교했을 때, 저체중 출생(평균 위험비(RR) 0.82; 95% 신뢰구간(CI) 0.55 to 1.22; 참여자 = 1898명; 연구 = 여덟 개; 낮은 질 근거), 영아 출생체중(평균차(MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; 참여자 = 1939명; 연구 = 아홉 개; 낮은 질 근거), 조산(평균 RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; 참여자 = 1177명; 연구 = 다섯 개; 낮은 질 근거), 신생아 사망(평균 RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; 참여자 = 795명; 연구 = 한 개; 매우 낮은 질 근거) 등 어떤 주요 영아 결과에서도 집단 간 차이에 대한 명확한 근거가 없었다.

evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Anaemia is a frequent condition during pregnancy, particularly among women in low- and middle-income countries. | Traditionally, gestational anaemia has been prevented with daily iron supplements throughout pregnancy, but adherence to this regimen due to side effects, interrupted supply of the supplements, and concerns about safety among women with an adequate iron intake, have limited the use of this intervention. | OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of intermittent supplementation with iron alone or in combination with folic acid or other vitamins and minerals to pregnant women on neonatal and pregnancy outcomes.

all_evidence.title: Vitamin D deficiency in pregnant women: obstetric implications and clinical management.
all_evidence.authors: Tadros-Zins M; Krekora M; Zych-Krekora K; Drosdzol-Cop A
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: This review analyzes current evidence regarding vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy from an obstetric perspective, focusing on pregnancy complications, fetal outcomes, and evidence-based supplementation strategies for clinical practice. | RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 분석 결과, 비타민 D 결핍(< 50 nmol/L)과 자간전증(OR 0.65), 임신성 당뇨병(OR 1.61), 조산(RR 0.67), 재태연령 대비 저체중 신생아(RR 0.61)의 위험 증가 사이에 유의한 연관성이 확인되었다.

all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 비타민 C를 단독 또는 다른 보충제와 함께 섭취한 여성은 위약 또는 무처치 대조군과 비교했을 때 사산(위험비(RR) 1.15, 95% 신뢰구간(CI) 0.89 to 1.49; 참여자 20,038명; 11개 연구; I² = 0%; 중등도 질 근거), 신생아 사망(RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.08; 참여자 19,575명; 11개 연구; I² = 0%), 주산기 사망(평균 RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.49; 참여자 17,105명; 일곱 개 연구; I² = 35%), 출생체중(평균차(MD) 26.88 g, 95% CI -18.81 to 72.58; 참여자 17,326명; 13개 연구; I² = 69%), 자궁내 성장 제한(RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.06; 참여자 20,361명; 12개 연구; I² = 15%; 높은 질 근거), 조산(평균 RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.10; 참여자 22,250명; 16개 연구; I² = 49%; 높은 질 근거), 조산 전 조기 양막파수(PROM, prelabour rupture of membranes)(평균 RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.36; 참여자 16,825명; 10개 연구; I² = 70%; 낮은 질 근거), 만삭 조기 양막파수(PROM)(평균 RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.62 to 2.56; 참여자 2674명; 세 개 연구; I² = 87%), 임상적 자간전증(평균 RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.05; 참여자 21,956명; 16개 연구; I² = 41%; 높은 질 근거) 위험에서 뚜렷한 차이가 없었다. 반면 위약 또는 무처치 대조군과 비교했을 때 태반조기박리 위험은 감소했고(RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.92; 참여자 15,755명; 여덟 개 연구; I² = 0%; 높은 질 근거), 출산 시 재태기간은 소폭 증가했으나(MD 0.31, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.61; 참여자 14,062명; 아홉 개 연구; I² = 65%), 복통을 자가 보고할 가능성도 더 높았다(RR 1.66, 95% CI 1.16 to 2.37; 참여자 1877명; 한 개 연구).

all_evidence.title: Intermittent oral iron supplementation during pregnancy.
all_evidence.authors: Peña-Rosas JP; De-Regil LM; Gomez Malave H; Flores-Urrutia MC; Dowswell T
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.outcome: None of the studies reported congenital anomalies.For maternal outcomes, there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for anaemia at term (average RR 1.22; 95% CI 0.84 to 1.80; participants = 676; studies = four; I² = 10%; very low quality). | There were no clear differences between groups for mean birthweight, preterm birth, maternal anaemia or maternal side effects.
all_evidence.key_finding: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 포함된 연구의 방법론적 질은 일관되지 않았고, 대부분 탈락률이 높았다. 주요 영아 결과에 관한 근거의 전반적 질은 낮았으며, 산모 결과에 관한 근거의 질은 매우 낮았다. 자료를 제공한 21개 시험 중 세 연구는 간헐적 철분 단독 요법, 14개 연구는 간헐적 철분 + 엽산 요법, 네 연구는 간헐적 철분과 복합 비타민·미네랄 요법을 각각 동일 조성의 일일 보충 요법과 비교했다. 전체적으로 간헐적 철분 요법(다른 비타민과 미네랄의 병용 여부 무관)을 받은 여성과 일일 요법을 받은 여성을 비교했을 때, 저체중 출생(평균 위험비(RR) 0.82; 95% 신뢰구간(CI) 0.55 to 1.22; 참여자 = 1898명; 연구 = 여덟 개; 낮은 질 근거), 영아 출생체중(평균차(MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; 참여자 = 1939명; 연구 = 아홉 개; 낮은 질 근거), 조산(평균 RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; 참여자 = 1177명; 연구 = 다섯 개; 낮은 질 근거), 신생아 사망(평균 RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; 참여자 = 795명; 연구 = 한 개; 매우 낮은 질 근거) 등 어떤 주요 영아 결과에서도 집단 간 차이에 대한 명확한 근거가 없었다.

all_evidence.title: The effects of oral ferrous bisglycinate supplementation on hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations in adults and children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.authors: Fischer JAJ; Cherian AM; Bone JN; Karakochuk CD
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).
all_evidence.outcome: Iron salts are commonly provided as oral supplements to prevent and treat iron deficiency, despite poor bioavailability and frequently reported adverse side effects. | Ferrous bisglycinate is a novel amino acid iron chelate that is thought to be more bioavailable and associated with fewer gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events as compared with iron salts. | OBJECTIVE: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted to evaluate the effects of ferrous bisglycinate supplementation compared with other iron supplements on hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations and GI adverse events.
all_evidence.key_finding: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 자료 분석: 다른 철분 보충제와 비교했을 때, 4-20주 동안 철 비스글리시네이트를 보충한 임신부는 헤모글로빈 농도가 더 높았고(SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% 신뢰구간[CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01), 보고된 위장관 이상반응은 더 적었다(IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).

evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: Analysis demonstrated significant associations between vitamin D deficiency (< 50 nmol/L) and elevated risk of preeclampsia (OR 0.65), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR 1.61), preterm birth (RR 0.67), and small-for-gestational-age neonates (RR 0.61).

all_evidence.title: Intermittent oral iron supplementation during pregnancy.
all_evidence.authors: Peña-Rosas JP; De-Regil LM; Gomez Malave H; Flores-Urrutia MC; Dowswell T
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.outcome: None of the studies reported congenital anomalies.For maternal outcomes, there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for anaemia at term (average RR 1.22; 95% CI 0.84 to 1.80; participants = 676; studies = four; I² = 10%; very low quality). | There were no clear differences between groups for mean birthweight, preterm birth, maternal anaemia or maternal side effects.
all_evidence.key_finding: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).

all_evidence.title: The effects of oral ferrous bisglycinate supplementation on hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations in adults and children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.authors: Fischer JAJ; Cherian AM; Bone JN; Karakochuk CD
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).
all_evidence.outcome: Iron salts are commonly provided as oral supplements to prevent and treat iron deficiency, despite poor bioavailability and frequently reported adverse side effects. | Ferrous bisglycinate is a novel amino acid iron chelate that is thought to be more bioavailable and associated with fewer gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events as compared with iron salts. | OBJECTIVE: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted to evaluate the effects of ferrous bisglycinate supplementation compared with other iron supplements on hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations and GI adverse events.
all_evidence.key_finding: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 자료 분석: 다른 철분 보충제와 비교했을 때, 4-20주 동안 철 비스글리시네이트를 보충한 임신부는 헤모글로빈 농도가 더 높았고(SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% 신뢰구간[CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01), 보고된 위장관 이상반응은 더 적었다(IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).

evidence.title: The effects of progesterone supplementation in pregnancies assessed by doppler ultrasound: a systematic review of maternal and perinatal outcomes.

evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_12: CONCLUSIONS: Progesterone supplementation in early and mid-pregnancy may benefit certain subgroups, particularly those at risk of preterm birth.

evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Progesterone is essential for pregnancy maintenance, but its effects on complications like intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), preeclampsia, prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM), preterm birth, and placental abruption are still debated. | This review investigates the effects of progesterone supplementation on Doppler ultrasound indices and pregnancy outcomes. | MATERIAL AND METHODS: To assess the efficacy of progesterone supplements in reducing pregnancy complications during the first and second trimesters using Doppler ultrasound indices.

all_evidence.title: Intermittent oral iron supplementation during pregnancy.

all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.outcome: None of the studies reported congenital anomalies.For maternal outcomes, there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for anaemia at term (average RR 1.22; 95% CI 0.84 to 1.80; participants = 676; studies = four; I² = 10%; very low quality). | There were no clear differences between groups for mean birthweight, preterm birth, maternal anaemia or maternal side effects.

evidence.title: Profile of herbal and dietary supplements induced liver injury in Latin America: A systematic review of published reports.
evidence.authors: Santos G; Gasca J; Parana R; Nunes V; Schinnoni M; Medina-Caliz I; Cabello MR; Lucena MI; Andrade RJ
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_2: We have undertaken a systematic review of published case reports and case series from LA from 1976 to 2020 to describe the clinical features of HDS related hepatotoxicity in this region.
evidence.outcome: Hepatotoxicity related to HDS is a growing global health issue. | We have undertaken a systematic review of published case reports and case series from LA from 1976 to 2020 to describe the clinical features of HDS related hepatotoxicity in this region. | The clinical characteristics of HDS hepatotoxicity in our study were compared to those of other studies in the USA, Europe and China showing a similar signature with predominance of young females, hepatocellular damage, a high rate of ALF and mortality, more frequent inadvertent re-challenge and chronic damage.
evidence.key_finding: We have undertaken a systematic review of published case reports and case series from LA from 1976 to 2020 to describe the clinical features of HDS related hepatotoxicity in this region.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 이 지역에서 HDS 관련 간독성의 임상적 특징을 설명하기 위해 1976년부터 2020년까지 라틴아메리카(LA)에서 발표된 증례 보고와 증례군을 체계적으로 문헌 고찰했다.
evidence.population: The clinical characteristics of HDS hepatotoxicity in our study were compared to those of other studies in the USA, Europe and China showing a similar signature with predominance of young females, hepatocellular damage, a high rate of ALF and mortality, more frequent inadvertent re-challenge and chronic damage. | This study underscores the challenge in causality assessment when multi-ingredients HDS are taken and the need for consistent publication practice when reporting hepatotoxicity cases due to HDS, to foster HDS liver safety particularly in LA.

evidence.title: Acute liver injury following turmeric use in Tuscany: An analysis of the Italian Phytovigilance database and systematic review of case reports.

evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_2: The aim of this research was to describe the Tuscan (Italy) cases of acute hepatitis and to compare them with similar cases of hepatotoxicity published in the literature by performing a systematic review.

all_evidence.title: Effects of Delta-tocotrienol Supplementation on Liver Enzymes, Inflammation, Oxidative stress and Hepatic Steatosis in Patients with Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease.
all_evidence.authors: Pervez MA; Khan DA; Ijaz A; Khan S
all_evidence.venue: The Turkish journal of gastroenterology : the official journal of Turkish Society of Gastroenterology
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_12: CONCLUSION: δ-Tocotrienol was safe, and it effectively improved aminotransferase levels and inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in patients with NAFLD.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a growing public health problem worldwide and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. | Currently, there is no definitive treatment for this disease. δ-Tocotrienol has potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties and may reduce liver injury in NAFLD. | After 12 weeks of supplementation, δ-tocotrienol showed greater efficacy than placebo by decreasing serum aminotransferases, hs-CRP, MDA, and FLI score (p<0.001).
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSION: δ-Tocotrienol was safe, and it effectively improved aminotransferase levels and inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in patients with NAFLD.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 결론: δ-토코트리에놀은 안전했으며, NAFLD 환자의 아미노전이효소 수치와 염증 및 산화 스트레스 표지자를 효과적으로 개선했다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a growing public health problem worldwide and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. | Currently, there is no definitive treatment for this disease. δ-Tocotrienol has potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties and may reduce liver injury in NAFLD. | MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present study was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study conducted in patients aged > 20 years, belonging to both sexes, having ultrasound-proven fatty liver disease, having a fatty liver index (FLI) of ≥ 60, and persistent elevation of alanine transaminase.

all_evidence.title: Effect of curcumin supplementation on disease severity in patients with liver cirrhosis: A randomized controlled trial.
all_evidence.authors: Nouri-Vaskeh M; Malek Mahdavi A; Afshan H; Alizadeh L; Zarei M
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: MELD(i) (15.55 ± 3.78 to 12.41 ± 3.07), MELD (15.31 ± 3.07 to 12.03 ± 2.79), MELD-Na (15.97 ± 4.02 to 13.55 ± 3.51), and Child-Pugh (7.17 ± 1.54 to 6.72 ± 1.31) scores decreased significantly in the curcumin group after 3-month intervention (p < .001, p < .001, p = .001, and p = .051, respectively), whereas they increased significantly in the placebo group (p < .001, p < .001, p < .001, p = .001, respectively).
all_evidence.outcome: Recent reports indicated that curcumin had beneficial effects in animal models of liver injury and cirrhosis.
all_evidence.key_finding: MELD(i) (15.55 ± 3.78 to 12.41 ± 3.07), MELD (15.31 ± 3.07 to 12.03 ± 2.79), MELD-Na (15.97 ± 4.02 to 13.55 ± 3.51), and Child-Pugh (7.17 ± 1.54 to 6.72 ± 1.31) scores decreased significantly in the curcumin group after 3-month intervention (p < .001, p < .001, p = .001, and p = .051, respectively), whereas they increased significantly in the placebo group (p < .001, p < .001, p < .001, p = .001, respectively).
all_evidence.publication_types: Clinical Trial, Phase III|Journal Article|Randomized Controlled Trial
all_evidence.population: Recent reports indicated that curcumin had beneficial effects in animal models of liver injury and cirrhosis. | Current study aimed to investigate the effects of curcumin supplementation in patients with liver cirrhosis. | In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients with liver cirrhosis aged 20-70 years were randomly divided into two groups to receive 1,000 mg/day curcumin (n = 35) or placebo (n = 35) for 3 months.

evidence.title: Effect of Green Tea Supplements on Liver Enzyme Elevation: Results from a Randomized Intervention Study in the United States.
evidence.authors: Yu Z; Samavat H; Dostal AM; Wang R; Torkelson CJ; Yang CS; Butler LM; Kensler TW; Wu AH; Kurzer MS; Yuan JM
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_3: We examined the potential effects of a high, sustained oral dose of green tea extract (GTE) on liver injury measures in a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded phase II clinical trial, which enrolled 1,075 women with the original aim to assess the effect of daily GTE consumption for 12 months on biomarkers of breast cancer risk.
evidence.outcome: Liver injury effects of green tea-based products have been reported in sporadic case reports. | However, no study has examined systematically such adverse effects in an unbiased manner. | We examined the potential effects of a high, sustained oral dose of green tea extract (GTE) on liver injury measures in a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded phase II clinical trial, which enrolled 1,075 women with the original aim to assess the effect of daily GTE consumption for 12 months on biomarkers of breast cancer risk.
evidence.key_finding: We examined the potential effects of a high, sustained oral dose of green tea extract (GTE) on liver injury measures in a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded phase II clinical trial, which enrolled 1,075 women with the original aim to assess the effect of daily GTE consumption for 12 months on biomarkers of breast cancer risk.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 고용량 녹차 추출물(GTE)을 지속해서 경구 투여했을 때 간 손상 지표에 미칠 수 있는 영향을 무작위 배정, 위약 대조, 이중 눈가림 II상 임상시험에서 조사했다. 이 시험에는 여성 1,075명이 참여했으며, 원래 목적은 12개월 동안 매일 GTE를 섭취했을 때 유방암 위험 생체표지자에 미치는 영향을 평가하는 것이었다.
evidence.publication_types: Clinical Trial, Phase II|Journal Article|Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.population: Liver injury effects of green tea-based products have been reported in sporadic case reports. | We examined the potential effects of a high, sustained oral dose of green tea extract (GTE) on liver injury measures in a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded phase II clinical trial, which enrolled 1,075 women with the original aim to assess the effect of daily GTE consumption for 12 months on biomarkers of breast cancer risk. | The current analysis examined the effect of GTE consumption on liver injury in 1,021 participants (513 in GTE and 508 in placebo arm) with normal baseline levels of liver enzymes.

evidence.title: Milk thistle for alcoholic and/or hepatitis B or C liver diseases--a systematic cochrane hepato-biliary group review with meta-analyses of randomized clinical trials.
evidence.authors: Rambaldi A; Jacobs BP; Iaquinto G; Gluud C
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: MT versus placebo or no intervention for a median duration of 6 months had no significant effects on all-cause mortality (relative risk (RR) 0.78, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.53-1.15), complications of liver disease, or liver histology.
evidence.outcome: MT versus placebo or no intervention for a median duration of 6 months had no significant effects on all-cause mortality (relative risk (RR) 0.78, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.53-1.15), complications of liver disease, or liver histology. | Liver-related mortality was significantly reduced by MT in all trials (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.29-0.88), but not in high-quality trials (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.28-1.19). | MT was not associated with a significantly increased risk of adverse events.
evidence.key_finding: MT versus placebo or no intervention for a median duration of 6 months had no significant effects on all-cause mortality (relative risk (RR) 0.78, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.53-1.15), complications of liver disease, or liver histology.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 중앙값 6개월 동안 MT를 위약 또는 무중재와 비교했을 때 모든 원인 사망률(상대위험도(RR) 0.78, 95% 신뢰구간(CI) 0.53-1.15), 간질환 합병증 또는 간 조직학적 소견에 유의한 영향이 없었다.
evidence.population: OBJECTIVES: Our objectives were to assess the beneficial and harmful effects of milk thistle (MT) or MT constituents versus placebo or no intervention in patients with alcoholic liver disease and/or hepatitis B and/or C liver diseases. | METHODS: Randomized clinical trials studying patients with alcoholic and/or hepatitis B or C liver diseases were included (December 2003). | RESULTS: Thirteen randomized clinical trials assessed MT in 915 patients with alcoholic and/or hepatitis B or C liver diseases.

all_evidence.title: Clinically relevant interaction between warfarin and scuppernongs, a quercetin containing muscadine grape: continued questions surrounding flavonoid-induced warfarin interactions.
all_evidence.authors: Woodward CJ; Deyo ZM; Donahue KE; Deal AM; Hawes EM

all_evidence.outcome: We present a case of clinically relevant and probable interaction between warfarin and scuppernongs in a 73-year-old woman where ingestion of scuppernongs, a variety of quercetin-containing muscadine grapes, over a period of 2 months was associated with elevations in the International Normalised Ratio to supratherapeutic levels.

all_evidence.title: Analysis of Factors That Interrupt With INR Control in the First Anticoagulation Clinic Monitoring Jordanian Patients.
all_evidence.authors: Al-Momany NH; Makahleh ZM; Al-Omari NA; Al-Sarayreh HA; Momani RO
all_evidence.venue: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_17: Factors that interrupted INR control in our population, arranged in descending sequence, were concurrent medication use 46.9% (mainly Salicylates and Amiodarone), smoking cigarettes and shisha 17% (represented the most frequent single factor that caused non-TINR in the present study), a nonbalanced dietary vitamin K intake 16.88% caused changes in INR (lower) was related to an increase in the intake of vitamin K-rich food, were noticed to be much more in the spring season in Jordan (end of March and April mainly), herbal supplements 15.02%; Hawthorn (Crataegus, الزعرور) is an herb that lives widely in Jordan, and shockingly we found that it is used very commonly in our ACC patients and corresponded to an elevated INR <8 in 11 patients, and serious bleeding events that required hospitalization in 2 cases), noncompliance 1.49%, comorbid diseases 1%, malabsorption 0.53%, alcohol intake 0.39%, and VKORC1 A/G and CYP2C9 *1*1 genotype 0.15%.
all_evidence.outcome: Multiple factors such as vitamin K consumption, drug interactions, herbs interactions, disease states, and alcohol intake affect international normalized ratio (INR) values and thus warfarin dosing. | In contrast, the factors that affect INR control in a specific population are rarely studied. | Being aware of these factors contributes a lot in maintaining an INR control and avoiding the supratherapeutic or subtherapeutic anticoagulation and the associated risks of hemorrhage or thromboembolism.
all_evidence.key_finding: Factors that interrupted INR control in our population, arranged in descending sequence, were concurrent medication use 46.9% (mainly Salicylates and Amiodarone), smoking cigarettes and shisha 17% (represented the most frequent single factor that caused non-TINR in the present study), a nonbalanced dietary vitamin K intake 16.88% caused changes in INR (lower) was related to an increase in the intake of vitamin K-rich food, were noticed to be much more in the spring season in Jordan (end of March and April mainly), herbal supplements 15.02%; Hawthorn (Crataegus, الزعرور) is an herb that lives widely in Jordan, and shockingly we found that it is used very commonly in our ACC patients and corresponded to an elevated INR <8 in 11 patients, and serious bleeding events that required hospitalization in 2 cases), noncompliance 1.49%, comorbid diseases 1%, malabsorption 0.53%, alcohol intake 0.39%, and VKORC1 A/G and CYP2C9 *1*1 genotype 0.15%.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 연구 대상 집단에서 INR 조절을 방해한 요인을 빈도 내림차순으로 배열하면 병용 약물 사용 46.9%(주로 살리실산염과 아미오다론), 담배와 시샤 흡연 17%(본 연구에서 비목표 INR을 유발한 가장 흔한 단일 요인), 불균형한 식이 비타민 K 섭취 16.88%였다. 비타민 K가 풍부한 음식 섭취 증가와 관련해 INR이 낮아졌으며, 이는 요르단의 봄철(주로 삼월 말과 사월)에 훨씬 더 많이 관찰되었다. 허브 보충제는 15.02%였다. 산사나무(Crataegus, الزعرور)는 요르단 전역에 자라는 허브로, 놀랍게도 항응고 클리닉 환자들이 매우 흔히 사용했으며 환자 11명에서 INR <8 상승과 관련되었고, 2건에서는 입원이 필요한 중대한 출혈이 발생했다. 그 밖의 요인은 복약 불이행 1.49%, 동반 질환 1%, 흡수 장애 0.53%, 음주 0.39%, VKORC1 A/G 및 CYP2C9 *1*1 유전자형 0.15%였다.
all_evidence.population: Multiple factors such as vitamin K consumption, drug interactions, herbs interactions, disease states, and alcohol intake affect international normalized ratio (INR) values and thus warfarin dosing. | Being aware of these factors contributes a lot in maintaining an INR control and avoiding the supratherapeutic or subtherapeutic anticoagulation and the associated risks of hemorrhage or thromboembolism. | Alarming factors causing non-TINR detected in our study include smoking both cigarettes and shisha, herbal use (Hawthorn and Ginseng), increased intake of vitamin K rich food in the spring season, and concurrent medication use (Salicylates, Amiodarone, Ciprofloxacin, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDS], Azithromycin, Clarithromycin: although the use of these drugs is mandatory sometimes, it can be replaced by an alternative, eg, antibiotics or monitored closely together with warfarin).

all_evidence.venue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: In 35% of patients, we recommended stopping some of their DS or other therapies, the reasons being: DC antioxidants, vitamin B12/iron while on chemo/RT (unless deficient or part of protocol) 32%; DC due to taking excess amounts (i.e., fat-soluble vitamins, calcium, iron) 13.5%; DC supplements with known toxicity (i.e., laetrile, Miracle mineral solution) 13.5%; DC due to interactions with other medications (i.e., anticoagulants) 13.5%; DC DS with potential to increase cancer growth (i.e., estrogenic potential in those with hormone-sensitive cancers, glutamine) 11%; DC due to potential for increased toxicity with chemotherapy (i.e., increased risk of bleeding, CIPN) 11%; DC probiotics, immune stimulants, and cannabis while on immunotherapy 5.4%.

evidence.title: Vitamin K supplementation can improve stability of anticoagulation for patients with unexplained variability in response to warfarin.
evidence.authors: Sconce E; Avery P; Wynne H; Kamali F
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_5: Vitamin K supplementation resulted in a significantly greater decrease in standard deviation of international normalized ratio (INR) compared with placebo (-0.24 +/- 0.14 vs -0.11 +/- 0.18; P < .001) and a significantly greater increase in percentage time within target INR range (28% +/- 20% vs 15% +/- 20%; P < .01).
evidence.outcome: Patients receiving warfarin who have unstable control of anticoagulation have a significantly lower intake of dietary vitamin K compared with their stable counterparts. | We hypothesized that supplementation with oral vitamin K would improve stability in patients with previously unstable control of anticoagulation. | Seventy warfarin-treated patients with unstable anticoagulation control were randomly assigned in a double-blinded fashion to receive a daily amount of 150 mug oral vitamin K or placebo orally for 6 months.
evidence.key_finding: Vitamin K supplementation resulted in a significantly greater decrease in standard deviation of international normalized ratio (INR) compared with placebo (-0.24 +/- 0.14 vs -0.11 +/- 0.18; P < .001) and a significantly greater increase in percentage time within target INR range (28% +/- 20% vs 15% +/- 20%; P < .01).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 비타민 K 보충군은 위약군보다 국제정상화비율(INR) 표준편차가 유의하게 더 크게 감소했고(-0.24 +/- 0.14 vs -0.11 +/- 0.18; P < .001), 목표 INR 범위 안에 있었던 시간의 비율도 유의하게 더 크게 증가했다(28% +/- 20% vs 15% +/- 20%; P < .01).
evidence.population: Patients receiving warfarin who have unstable control of anticoagulation have a significantly lower intake of dietary vitamin K compared with their stable counterparts. | We hypothesized that supplementation with oral vitamin K would improve stability in patients with previously unstable control of anticoagulation. | Seventy warfarin-treated patients with unstable anticoagulation control were randomly assigned in a double-blinded fashion to receive a daily amount of 150 mug oral vitamin K or placebo orally for 6 months.

evidence.title: Interaction Between Dietary Vitamin K Intake and Anticoagulation by Vitamin K Antagonists: Is It Really True?: A Systematic Review.
evidence.authors: Violi F; Lip GY; Pignatelli P; Pastori D
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_4: We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included.
evidence.outcome: Common belief is that dietary vitamin K intake could counteract the anticoagulant effect by VKAs and for many years, patients have been discouraged to consume vitamin-K-rich foods, such as green leafy vegetables.The objective of this study is to summarize the current evidence supporting the putative interaction between dietary vitamin K intake and changes in INR with the VKAs.Data sources are MEDLINE via PubMed and Cochrane database.All clinical studies investigating the relationship between dietary vitamin K and measures of anticoagulation were included. | We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included. | We found conflicting evidence on the effect of dietary intake of vitamin K on coagulation response.
evidence.key_finding: We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 비타민 K만 단독으로 보충한 모든 연구는 제외했다. 2015년 시월까지의 문헌을 대상으로 체계적 문헌고찰을 수행했으며, "food", "diet", "vitamin K", "phylloquinone", "warfarin", "INR", "coagulation", "anticoagulant"를 조합해 검색했다. 식이 중재시험 두 건과 관찰연구 9건을 포함했다.
evidence.population: Common belief is that dietary vitamin K intake could counteract the anticoagulant effect by VKAs and for many years, patients have been discouraged to consume vitamin-K-rich foods, such as green leafy vegetables.The objective of this study is to summarize the current evidence supporting the putative interaction between dietary vitamin K intake and changes in INR with the VKAs.Data sources are MEDLINE via PubMed and Cochrane database.All clinical studies investigating the relationship between dietary vitamin K and measures of anticoagulation were included. | We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included. | Some studies found a negative correlation between vitamin K intake and INR changes, while others suggested that a minimum amount of vitamin K is required to maintain an adequate anticoagulation.

evidence.title: Potential interactions between complementary/alternative products and conventional medicines in a Medicare population.
evidence.authors: Elmer GW; Lafferty WE; Tyree PT; Lind BK
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Of these, 294 (5.8%) individuals took combinations considered to have a significant risk for an adverse interaction.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Despite the high prevalence of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) product use among the elderly, little is known about the extent of concurrent CAM-conventional medicine use and the potential for adverse reactions. | OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of CAM product use concurrent with conventional medications, prescription and nonprescription, in a Medicare population and assess the risk for adverse interactions. | The adverse interaction risks were categorized as unknown, theoretical, and significant.
evidence.key_finding: Of these, 294 (5.8%) individuals took combinations considered to have a significant risk for an adverse interaction.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_17: Factors that interrupted INR control in our population, arranged in descending sequence, were concurrent medication use 46.9% (mainly Salicylates and Amiodarone), smoking cigarettes and shisha 17% (represented the most frequent single factor that caused non-TINR in the present study), a nonbalanced dietary vitamin K intake 16.88% caused changes in INR (lower) was related to an increase in the intake of vitamin K-rich food, were noticed to be much more in the spring season in Jordan (end of March and April mainly), herbal supplements 15.02%; Hawthorn (Crataegus, الزعرور) is an herb that lives widely in Jordan, and shockingly we found that it is used very commonly in our ACC patients and corresponded to an elevated INR <8 in 11 patients, and serious bleeding events that required hospitalization in 2 cases), noncompliance 1.49%, comorbid diseases 1%, malabsorption 0.53%, alcohol intake 0.39%, and VKORC1 A/G and CYP2C9 *1*1 genotype 0.15%.

all_evidence.title: Interaction Between Dietary Vitamin K Intake and Anticoagulation by Vitamin K Antagonists: Is It Really True?: A Systematic Review.
all_evidence.authors: Violi F; Lip GY; Pignatelli P; Pastori D
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_4: We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included.
all_evidence.outcome: Common belief is that dietary vitamin K intake could counteract the anticoagulant effect by VKAs and for many years, patients have been discouraged to consume vitamin-K-rich foods, such as green leafy vegetables.The objective of this study is to summarize the current evidence supporting the putative interaction between dietary vitamin K intake and changes in INR with the VKAs.Data sources are MEDLINE via PubMed and Cochrane database.All clinical studies investigating the relationship between dietary vitamin K and measures of anticoagulation were included. | We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included. | We found conflicting evidence on the effect of dietary intake of vitamin K on coagulation response.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: Using the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) MedWatch database, 20 reports of glucosamine or glucosamine-chondroitin sulfate use with warfarin associated with altered coagulation (manifested by increased INR, or increased bleeding or bruising) were identified.
all_evidence.outcome: We describe a 71-year-old man who had received warfarin 7.5 mg/day for 5 years for atrial fibrillation, which had maintained his international normalized ratio (INR) within a narrow range of 2.5-3.2. | The patient then increased his dosage of glucosamine to 1500 mg and chondroitin to 1200 mg twice/day; his INR previous to this change was 2.3. | Approximately 3 weeks later, his INR increased to 3.9.

all_evidence.title: Analysis of Factors That Interrupt With INR Control in the First Anticoagulation Clinic Monitoring Jordanian Patients.
all_evidence.authors: Al-Momany NH; Makahleh ZM; Al-Omari NA; Al-Sarayreh HA; Momani RO
all_evidence.venue: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_17: Factors that interrupted INR control in our population, arranged in descending sequence, were concurrent medication use 46.9% (mainly Salicylates and Amiodarone), smoking cigarettes and shisha 17% (represented the most frequent single factor that caused non-TINR in the present study), a nonbalanced dietary vitamin K intake 16.88% caused changes in INR (lower) was related to an increase in the intake of vitamin K-rich food, were noticed to be much more in the spring season in Jordan (end of March and April mainly), herbal supplements 15.02%; Hawthorn (Crataegus, الزعرور) is an herb that lives widely in Jordan, and shockingly we found that it is used very commonly in our ACC patients and corresponded to an elevated INR <8 in 11 patients, and serious bleeding events that required hospitalization in 2 cases), noncompliance 1.49%, comorbid diseases 1%, malabsorption 0.53%, alcohol intake 0.39%, and VKORC1 A/G and CYP2C9 *1*1 genotype 0.15%.
all_evidence.outcome: Multiple factors such as vitamin K consumption, drug interactions, herbs interactions, disease states, and alcohol intake affect international normalized ratio (INR) values and thus warfarin dosing. | In contrast, the factors that affect INR control in a specific population are rarely studied. | Being aware of these factors contributes a lot in maintaining an INR control and avoiding the supratherapeutic or subtherapeutic anticoagulation and the associated risks of hemorrhage or thromboembolism.
all_evidence.key_finding: Factors that interrupted INR control in our population, arranged in descending sequence, were concurrent medication use 46.9% (mainly Salicylates and Amiodarone), smoking cigarettes and shisha 17% (represented the most frequent single factor that caused non-TINR in the present study), a nonbalanced dietary vitamin K intake 16.88% caused changes in INR (lower) was related to an increase in the intake of vitamin K-rich food, were noticed to be much more in the spring season in Jordan (end of March and April mainly), herbal supplements 15.02%; Hawthorn (Crataegus, الزعرور) is an herb that lives widely in Jordan, and shockingly we found that it is used very commonly in our ACC patients and corresponded to an elevated INR <8 in 11 patients, and serious bleeding events that required hospitalization in 2 cases), noncompliance 1.49%, comorbid diseases 1%, malabsorption 0.53%, alcohol intake 0.39%, and VKORC1 A/G and CYP2C9 *1*1 genotype 0.15%.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 연구 대상 집단에서 INR 조절을 방해한 요인을 빈도 내림차순으로 배열하면 병용 약물 사용 46.9%(주로 살리실산염과 아미오다론), 담배와 시샤 흡연 17%(본 연구에서 비목표 INR을 유발한 가장 흔한 단일 요인), 불균형한 식이 비타민 K 섭취 16.88%였다. 비타민 K가 풍부한 음식 섭취 증가와 관련해 INR이 낮아졌으며, 이는 요르단의 봄철(주로 삼월 말과 사월)에 훨씬 더 많이 관찰되었다. 허브 보충제는 15.02%였다. 산사나무(Crataegus, الزعرور)는 요르단 전역에 자라는 허브로, 놀랍게도 항응고 클리닉 환자들이 매우 흔히 사용했으며 환자 11명에서 INR <8 상승과 관련되었고, 2건에서는 입원이 필요한 중대한 출혈이 발생했다. 그 밖의 요인은 복약 불이행 1.49%, 동반 질환 1%, 흡수 장애 0.53%, 음주 0.39%, VKORC1 A/G 및 CYP2C9 *1*1 유전자형 0.15%였다.
all_evidence.population: Multiple factors such as vitamin K consumption, drug interactions, herbs interactions, disease states, and alcohol intake affect international normalized ratio (INR) values and thus warfarin dosing. | Being aware of these factors contributes a lot in maintaining an INR control and avoiding the supratherapeutic or subtherapeutic anticoagulation and the associated risks of hemorrhage or thromboembolism. | Alarming factors causing non-TINR detected in our study include smoking both cigarettes and shisha, herbal use (Hawthorn and Ginseng), increased intake of vitamin K rich food in the spring season, and concurrent medication use (Salicylates, Amiodarone, Ciprofloxacin, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDS], Azithromycin, Clarithromycin: although the use of these drugs is mandatory sometimes, it can be replaced by an alternative, eg, antibiotics or monitored closely together with warfarin).

all_evidence.authors: D'Andre SD; Bauer BA; Hofmann MB; Burckhard JL; Montane HN; Loprinzi CL
all_evidence.venue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: In 35% of patients, we recommended stopping some of their DS or other therapies, the reasons being: DC antioxidants, vitamin B12/iron while on chemo/RT (unless deficient or part of protocol) 32%; DC due to taking excess amounts (i.e., fat-soluble vitamins, calcium, iron) 13.5%; DC supplements with known toxicity (i.e., laetrile, Miracle mineral solution) 13.5%; DC due to interactions with other medications (i.e., anticoagulants) 13.5%; DC DS with potential to increase cancer growth (i.e., estrogenic potential in those with hormone-sensitive cancers, glutamine) 11%; DC due to potential for increased toxicity with chemotherapy (i.e., increased risk of bleeding, CIPN) 11%; DC probiotics, immune stimulants, and cannabis while on immunotherapy 5.4%.
all_evidence.outcome: There is potential for harm in several ways: (1) interactions with their medications that may increase side effects, (2) interactions with their treatment that may lead to decreased efficacy, and 3) direct toxicity from the supplement. | In 35% of patients, we recommended stopping some of their DS or other therapies, the reasons being: DC antioxidants, vitamin B12/iron while on chemo/RT (unless deficient or part of protocol) 32%; DC due to taking excess amounts (i.e., fat-soluble vitamins, calcium, iron) 13.5%; DC supplements with known toxicity (i.e., laetrile, Miracle mineral solution) 13.5%; DC due to interactions with other medications (i.e., anticoagulants) 13.5%; DC DS with potential to increase cancer growth (i.e., estrogenic potential in those with hormone-sensitive cancers, glutamine) 11%; DC due to potential for increased toxicity with chemotherapy (i.e., increased risk of bleeding, CIPN) 11%; DC probiotics, immune stimulants, and cannabis while on immunotherapy 5.4%. | CONCLUSIONS: Patients with cancer referred to an integrative oncology clinic use large numbers of DS with the potential for adverse effects and/or decreasing efficacy of treatments.

evidence.title: Over-the-counter vitamin K1-containing multivitamin supplements disrupt warfarin anticoagulation in vitamin K1-depleted patients. A prospective, controlled trial.
evidence.authors: Kurnik D; Loebstein R; Rabinovitz H; Austerweil N; Halkin H; Almog S
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: We conclude that vitamin K(1)-containing multivitamins reduce INR in patients with low vitamin K(1) status.
evidence.outcome: Most multivitamin supplements contain far less vitamin K(1) than thought to affect warfarin anticoagulation. | Having described 3 patients with multivitamin-warfarin interactions, we hypothesized that vitamin K(1)-depleted patients are sensitive to even small increments. | Therefore, we compared the effect of a vitamin K(1)-containing multivitamin on warfarin anticoagulation between patients with low versus normal vitamin K(1) status.
evidence.key_finding: We conclude that vitamin K(1)-containing multivitamins reduce INR in patients with low vitamin K(1) status.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 비타민 K(1)이 함유된 종합비타민은 비타민 K(1) 상태가 낮은 환자의 INR을 낮춘다고 결론지었다.
evidence.population: Most multivitamin supplements contain far less vitamin K(1) than thought to affect warfarin anticoagulation. | Having described 3 patients with multivitamin-warfarin interactions, we hypothesized that vitamin K(1)-depleted patients are sensitive to even small increments. | Therefore, we compared the effect of a vitamin K(1)-containing multivitamin on warfarin anticoagulation between patients with low versus normal vitamin K(1) status.

evidence.title: Interaction Between Dietary Vitamin K Intake and Anticoagulation by Vitamin K Antagonists: Is It Really True?: A Systematic Review.
evidence.authors: Violi F; Lip GY; Pignatelli P; Pastori D
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_4: We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included.
evidence.outcome: Common belief is that dietary vitamin K intake could counteract the anticoagulant effect by VKAs and for many years, patients have been discouraged to consume vitamin-K-rich foods, such as green leafy vegetables.The objective of this study is to summarize the current evidence supporting the putative interaction between dietary vitamin K intake and changes in INR with the VKAs.Data sources are MEDLINE via PubMed and Cochrane database.All clinical studies investigating the relationship between dietary vitamin K and measures of anticoagulation were included. | We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included. | We found conflicting evidence on the effect of dietary intake of vitamin K on coagulation response.
evidence.key_finding: We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 비타민 K만 단독으로 보충한 모든 연구는 제외했다. 2015년 시월까지의 문헌을 대상으로 체계적 문헌고찰을 수행했으며, "food", "diet", "vitamin K", "phylloquinone", "warfarin", "INR", "coagulation", "anticoagulant"를 조합해 검색했다. 식이 중재시험 두 건과 관찰연구 9건을 포함했다.
evidence.population: Common belief is that dietary vitamin K intake could counteract the anticoagulant effect by VKAs and for many years, patients have been discouraged to consume vitamin-K-rich foods, such as green leafy vegetables.The objective of this study is to summarize the current evidence supporting the putative interaction between dietary vitamin K intake and changes in INR with the VKAs.Data sources are MEDLINE via PubMed and Cochrane database.All clinical studies investigating the relationship between dietary vitamin K and measures of anticoagulation were included. | We excluded all studies of supplementation of vitamin K alone.We performed a systematic review of the literature up to October 2015, searching for a combination of "food," "diet," "vitamin K," "phylloquinone," "warfarin," "INR," "coagulation," and "anticoagulant."Two dietary interventional trials and 9 observational studies were included. | Some studies found a negative correlation between vitamin K intake and INR changes, while others suggested that a minimum amount of vitamin K is required to maintain an adequate anticoagulation.

evidence.title: Potential glucosamine-warfarin interaction resulting in increased international normalized ratio: case report and review of the literature and MedWatch database.
evidence.authors: Knudsen JF; Sokol GH
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: Using the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) MedWatch database, 20 reports of glucosamine or glucosamine-chondroitin sulfate use with warfarin associated with altered coagulation (manifested by increased INR, or increased bleeding or bruising) were identified.
evidence.outcome: We describe a 71-year-old man who had received warfarin 7.5 mg/day for 5 years for atrial fibrillation, which had maintained his international normalized ratio (INR) within a narrow range of 2.5-3.2. | The patient then increased his dosage of glucosamine to 1500 mg and chondroitin to 1200 mg twice/day; his INR previous to this change was 2.3. | Approximately 3 weeks later, his INR increased to 3.9.
evidence.key_finding: Using the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) MedWatch database, 20 reports of glucosamine or glucosamine-chondroitin sulfate use with warfarin associated with altered coagulation (manifested by increased INR, or increased bleeding or bruising) were identified.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 미국 식품의약국(FDA) MedWatch 데이터베이스를 이용해, 응고 변화(INR 증가 또는 출혈이나 멍 증가로 나타남)와 관련하여 와파린과 글루코사민 또는 글루코사민-콘드로이틴 황산염을 함께 사용한 보고 20건을 확인했다.
evidence.population: We describe a 71-year-old man who had received warfarin 7.5 mg/day for 5 years for atrial fibrillation, which had maintained his international normalized ratio (INR) within a narrow range of 2.5-3.2. | The supplement was then stopped, and his warfarin schedule was changed to 7.5 mg every other day alternating with 3.75 mg every other day. | This case report suggests that a potential interaction exists between warfarin and glucosamine that is associated with an increase in the INR.

evidence.title: Evaluation of documented drug interactions and contraindications associated with herbs and dietary supplements: a systematic literature review.
evidence.authors: Tsai HH; Lin HW; Simon Pickard A; Tsai HY; Mahady GB
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_13: The findings would facilitate the health-care professionals to communicate these documented interactions and contraindications to their patients and/or caregivers thereby preventing serious adverse events and improving desired therapeutic outcomes.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The use of herbs and dietary supplements (HDS) alone or concomitantly with medications can potentially increase the risk of adverse events experienced by the patients. | This review aims to evaluate the documented HDS-drug interactions and contraindications. | RESULTS: While 85 primary literatures, six books and two web sites were reviewed for a total of 1,491 unique pairs of HDS-drug interactions, 213 HDS entities and 509 medications were involved.
evidence.key_finding: The findings would facilitate the health-care professionals to communicate these documented interactions and contraindications to their patients and/or caregivers thereby preventing serious adverse events and improving desired therapeutic outcomes.

evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
